attributes.name: aml_screening_status
attributes.description: Status of AML (Anti-Money Laundering) screening performed on this clearing record. Indicates whether the transaction has been cleared, flagged for review, is pending screening, or has been escalated for investigation.

attributes.name: clearing_confirmation_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the clearing house confirmed acceptance or rejection of the clearing submission. Marks the completion of the clearing validation phase.

attributes.name: clearing_cycle_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific clearing cycle or batch window in which this clearing record was processed. Clearing houses typically operate multiple cycles per day.
attributes.references: NACHA Operating Rules, Federal Reserve Operating Circulars

attributes.name: clearing_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged by the clearing house for processing this clearing record. May be a flat fee per transaction or a percentage of the cleared amount.

attributes.name: clearing_message_type
attributes.description: Type of clearing message or instruction format used. Examples include SWIFT MT message types (MT103, MT202), ISO 20022 message types (pacs.008, pacs.009), or proprietary clearing formats.

attributes.name: clearing_participant_identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the financial institution participating in the clearing process. May be a BIC (Bank Identifier Code), ABA routing number, or clearing house member identifier.
attributes.references: ISO 9362 (BIC), Federal Reserve ABA Routing Number

attributes.name: clearing_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique reference number assigned by the clearing house to identify this clearing submission. Business identifier for external reconciliation and inquiry.

attributes.name: clearing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the clearing record. Indicates whether the clearing submission has been accepted, rejected, is pending processing, or has progressed to settlement.

attributes.name: clearing_submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the payment instruction or batch was submitted to the clearing house for processing. Represents the business event time of clearing initiation.

attributes.name: collateral_requirement_amount
attributes.description: Amount of collateral required to be posted to the clearing house to cover settlement risk exposure. Common in securities clearing and derivatives clearing.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures

attributes.name: counterparty_participant_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the counterparty financial institution on the other side of the clearing transaction. Used in bilateral netting and settlement reconciliation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this clearing record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: cross_border_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this clearing record involves cross-border payment flows between different countries or currency zones. Relevant for FATCA (Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act) and CRS (Common Reporting Standard) compliance.

attributes.name: foreign_exchange_rate
attributes.description: Exchange rate applied for cross-currency clearing and settlement, particularly relevant for CLS (Continuous Linked Settlement) FX transactions. Represents the rate at which one currency is converted to another.

attributes.name: funding_account_number
attributes.description: Account number of the nostro, vostro, or settlement account used to fund the net settlement obligation or receive settlement proceeds. Typically a central bank account or correspondent banking account.

attributes.name: gross_clearing_amount
attributes.description: Total gross amount of all payment instructions included in this clearing record before any netting or offsetting. Represents the sum of all individual payment values submitted.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this clearing record was last updated or modified. Audit field for change tracking and data governance.

attributes.name: liquidity_reserve_requirement_amount
attributes.description: Amount of liquidity reserves that must be maintained to cover this clearing obligation. Relevant for regulatory liquidity management and LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio) calculations.
attributes.references: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR), Federal Reserve Regulation D

attributes.name: multilateral_netting_position
attributes.description: Indicates whether the institution is a net payer (owes funds), net receiver (receives funds), or neutral (no net obligation) after multilateral netting across all participants in the clearing cycle.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures

attributes.name: net_settlement_obligation_amount
attributes.description: Net settlement obligation amount after multilateral or bilateral netting has been applied by the clearing house. This is the actual amount that must be funded or will be received in the settlement phase.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures

attributes.name: netting_group_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the netting group or pool to which this clearing record belongs. Used in multilateral netting arrangements where participants are grouped for offset calculation.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures

attributes.name: nostro_vostro_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the settlement account is a nostro account (our account held at another bank), vostro account (their account held at our bank), or an internal account. Critical for correspondent banking reconciliation.

attributes.name: payment_instruction_count
attributes.description: Number of individual payment instructions included in this clearing record. Relevant for batch clearing submissions where multiple payments are cleared together.

attributes.name: priority_indicator
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to this clearing record. High-priority payments may be processed in earlier clearing cycles or given preferential treatment in settlement queues.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this clearing record must be included in regulatory reporting submissions such as CCAR (Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review), DFAST (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing), or other supervisory reports.

attributes.name: rejection_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the reason for clearing rejection if the clearing status is rejected. Examples include insufficient funds, invalid account, format errors, or compliance holds.
attributes.references: ISO 20022 External Code Lists, NACHA Return Reason Codes

attributes.name: rejection_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the reason for clearing rejection, providing additional context beyond the standardized rejection reason code.

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_status
attributes.description: Status of sanctions screening against OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control) and other sanctions lists. Indicates whether the transaction has been cleared, matched a sanctions list (hit), is pending review, or has been manually overridden.

attributes.name: settlement_confirmation_reference
attributes.description: Unique reference number provided by the settlement system confirming that final funds movement has been completed. Used for reconciliation and audit trail.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which final settlement of funds is scheduled to occur. Typically follows T+0, T+1, or T+2 convention depending on the payment system and instrument type.

attributes.name: settlement_method
attributes.description: Method used for final settlement of the net obligation. RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement) settles each transaction individually in real-time. DNS (Deferred Net Settlement) settles net positions at scheduled intervals. Hybrid combines both approaches.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures

attributes.name: settlement_risk_exposure_amount
attributes.description: Calculated settlement risk exposure amount representing the potential loss if the counterparty fails to settle. Used for credit risk management and regulatory capital calculations.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: Final status of the settlement process. Indicates whether funds have been successfully transferred, settlement failed, or the transaction was reversed or suspended.

attributes.name: settlement_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when final settlement of funds was completed and confirmed by the clearing house or settlement system. Marks the irrevocable transfer of funds.

attributes.name: settlement_window_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific settlement window or time slot in which final settlement is scheduled. Clearing houses may operate multiple settlement windows throughout the day.

attributes.name: source_system_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the source system that originated this clearing record. Examples include ACI Worldwide, Volante, or internal payment processing platforms. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

products.name: routing
products.description: Defines the routing rules and correspondent banking paths used to direct payments to their destination across all supported payment rails. Captures routing rule identifier, payment rail code (ACH/wire/RTGS/SWIFT/card), rail settlement model (gross/net), settlement cycle, cut-off times, destination country/currency, correspondent bank BIC, intermediary bank BIC, routing priority, velocity limits, approval thresholds, effective date range, and rule status. Sourced from SWIFT Reference Data (BIC directory, SSI registry) and Volante payment hub routing engine. Enables dynamic routing decisions based on cost, speed, liquidity position, and regulatory requirements.

products.name: payment_mandate

Captures mandate reference, mandate type (SEPA Core, SEPA B2B, ACH PPD/CCD), creditor identifier, debtor account, maximum amount, frequency, start date, end date, mandate status, and presentment sequence (first/recurring/final/one-off/re-presentment). Supports mandate amendment, cancellation, and dispute workflows. SSOT for pre-authorized payment agreements and direct debit lifecycle management.

products.name: reconciliation_item
products.description: This association product represents the matching Event between a reconciliation run and a specific payment transaction. It captures the operational outcome of matching one payment transaction within one reconciliation cycle, including match status, matched amount, sequence, and exception indicators. Each record is created by the reconciliation engine when it processes a transaction against an external statement, and is updated as breaks are investigated and resolved. This is the SSOT for per-transaction reconciliation outcomes.. Existence Justification: In payment operations, reconciliation is a batch process that matches multiple payment transactions against external clearing/settlement statements. A single reconciliation run covers many transactions, and critically, the same transaction can appear across multiple reconciliation cycles (initial, amended, final) — meaning the relationship is genuinely bidirectional and many-to-many. The business actively manages 'reconciliation items' — named operational records that capture the matching result (match_status, exception_flag, matched_amount, reconciliation_sequence) for each specific transaction within each specific reconciliation run.

attributes.name: reconciliation_item_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific payment transaction being matched in this reconciliation run.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the reconciliation run in which this transaction was processed.

attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this reconciliation item raised an exception during the matching process, requiring manual investigation or escalation by the reconciliation team.

attributes.name: match_status
attributes.description: The outcome of the matching process for this specific transaction within this reconciliation run. Indicates whether the transaction was fully matched, partially matched, unmatched (break), or subsequently resolved.

attributes.name: matched_amount
attributes.description: The monetary value confirmed as matched between the internal payment transaction record and the external statement entry for this specific reconciliation item. May differ from the transaction amount in partial match scenarios.

attributes.name: reconciliation_sequence
attributes.description: Indicates which cycle of the reconciliation process this item belongs to — initial run, amended run (after additional statement data arrives), or final run (after all breaks are resolved). Enables tracking of a transaction across multiple reconciliation cycles.

attributes.description: Indicates whether the derivative is cleared through a central counterparty (CCP) or remains bilateral between counterparties. Cleared derivatives have lower capital requirements under Basel III.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the derivative instrument record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: cusip
attributes.business_glossary_term: Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures (CUSIP)
attributes.description: 9-character alphanumeric code identifying North American securities. Used for clearing and settlement.

attributes.name: cva_amount
attributes.description: Adjustment to the mark-to-market value reflecting the counterparty credit risk. Calculated based on probability of default (PD), loss given default (LGD), and exposure at default (EAD).

attributes.name: derivative_type
attributes.description: Classification of the derivative instrument by contract structure: swap, forward, future, option, swaption, credit default swap (CDS), total return swap, variance swap, or exotic derivative. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: swap|forward|future|option|swaption|credit_default_swap|total_return_swap|variance_swap|exotic — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the derivative contract becomes legally binding and cash flows or obligations begin to accrue. May differ from trade date for forward-starting contracts.

attributes.name: exercise_style
attributes.description: Defines when the option holder can exercise the contract: European (only at expiry), American (any time before expiry), Bermudan (on specific dates), or Asian (based on average price over period).

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The last date on which an option can be exercised. Synonymous with maturity date for options but distinct for other derivative types.

attributes.name: frtb_capital_charge
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) Capital Charge
attributes.description: Market risk capital requirement calculated under the FRTB framework using either the standardized approach (SA) or internal models approach (IMA).

attributes.name: initial_margin
attributes.description: Collateral posted at trade inception to cover potential future exposure. Required for non-cleared derivatives under EMIR and Dodd-Frank margin rules.

attributes.name: isin
attributes.description: 12-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the derivative instrument globally. Used for regulatory reporting and trade repository submissions.

attributes.name: lifecycle_status
attributes.description: Current state of the derivative contract: active (live and accruing), matured (reached expiry), terminated (early termination), cancelled (voided before effective date), or suspended (temporarily inactive).

attributes.name: margin_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which initial and variation margin are posted.

attributes.name: mark_to_market_value
attributes.description: Current fair value of the derivative contract based on prevailing market prices and valuation models. Updated daily for profit and loss (PnL) attribution and CVA calculation.

attributes.name: maturity_date
attributes.description: The date on which the derivative contract expires and final settlement occurs. For options, this is the expiry date; for swaps, this is the termination date.

attributes.name: mtm_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the mark-to-market value is denominated.

attributes.name: notional_amount
attributes.description: The notional or face value of the derivative contract used to calculate payment obligations. Does not represent actual cash exchanged at inception but is the basis for calculating periodic settlements.

attributes.name: rwa_amount
attributes.description: Capital requirement for the derivative calculated under Basel III standardized approach (SA) or internal ratings-based (IRB) approach. Used for regulatory capital adequacy reporting.

attributes.name: sedol
attributes.description: 7-character alphanumeric code identifying securities traded on the London Stock Exchange and other UK exchanges.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which cash or physical settlement of the derivative contract occurs. Typically T+1 or T+2 after trade date depending on asset class and market convention.

attributes.name: settlement_type
attributes.description: Method of settlement at maturity: cash settlement (net cash payment based on market value) or physical delivery (actual transfer of underlying asset).

attributes.name: strike_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the strike price. Relevant for FX options and cross-currency derivatives.

attributes.name: strike_price
attributes.description: The predetermined price at which the holder of an option can buy (call) or sell (put) the underlying asset. Applicable to options, swaptions, and structured derivatives with embedded optionality.

attributes.name: subtype
attributes.description: Granular classification within the derivative type (e.g., interest rate swap, FX forward, equity call option, barrier option, Asian option). Provides detailed product categorization for risk and capital reporting.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the derivative contract was terminated early, either by mutual agreement or due to a credit event. Null for contracts that reach natural maturity.

attributes.name: trade_date
attributes.description: The date on which the derivative contract was executed and agreed upon by counterparties. Used for T+1 settlement calculations and trade repository reporting.

attributes.name: trade_repository_reference
attributes.description: Identifier assigned by the trade repository where the derivative transaction is reported under EMIR or Dodd-Frank regulations.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the derivative instrument record. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: uti
attributes.description: Globally unique identifier assigned to each derivative transaction for trade repository reporting under EMIR and Dodd-Frank regulations.

attributes.name: variation_margin
attributes.description: Daily collateral exchange based on mark-to-market movements. Ensures that counterparty exposure is fully collateralized on a daily basis.

products.name: issuer
products.description: Master data for security issuers including corporations, sovereign governments, municipalities, supranational entities, and special purpose vehicles (SPVs). Captures issuer legal name, LEI (Legal Entity Identifier), issuer type, domicile country, incorporation jurisdiction, parent entity, ultimate parent, credit ratings by agency, sector classification (GICS/SIC/NAICS), Bloomberg issuer ID, and regulatory classification (financial/non-financial). Serves as the authoritative issuer reference for fixed income, structured products, and credit risk domains. Distinct from the customer domain which owns client/counterparty identity.

attributes.name: issuer_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the security issuer. Primary key for the issuer master data product.

attributes.name: domicile_country_id

attributes.name: industry_code_id

attributes.name: jurisdiction_id

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Issuers that are bank subsidiaries or SPVs must be linked to the bank's legal entity registry for FINREP/COREP consolidation, intercompany elimination, and large exposure reporting. A banking regulato

attributes.name: lei_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.lei_registry. Business justification: Issuers must have LEI codes for MiFID II, EMIR, and SFTR regulatory reporting. issuer.lei is a plain text denormalization of the authoritative lei_registry entity. Compliance and regulatory reporting

attributes.name: parent_issuer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the immediate parent entity in the corporate hierarchy. Used for consolidated risk reporting and group exposure aggregation under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements, IFRS 10

attributes.name: primary_ultimate_parent_issuer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the top-level parent entity in the corporate hierarchy. Critical for ultimate risk aggregation, large exposure monitoring, and CCAR/DFAST stress testing.
attributes.references: Basel III Large Exposures Framework, CCAR Requirements, Federal Reserve SR 12-17

attributes.name: bloomberg_issuer_code
attributes.description: Bloomberg's proprietary issuer identifier used for market data integration, pricing feeds, and reference data synchronization with Bloomberg Terminal.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this issuer record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: cva_adjustment
attributes.description: The market value of counterparty credit risk for derivative exposures with this issuer. Required under Basel III CVA capital charge and IFRS 13 fair value accounting.
attributes.references: Basel III CVA Framework, IFRS 13, ISDA CVA Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this issuer record became effective in the system. Used for temporal queries and historical analysis.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Temporal Data Management

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this issuer record expires or was superseded. Null for currently active records. Supports slowly changing dimension Type 2 history.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, SCD Type 2 Pattern

attributes.name: fitch_issuer_rating
attributes.description: Current long-term issuer default rating assigned by Fitch Ratings. Provides third opinion for credit risk triangulation.
attributes.references: Fitch Ratings Definitions, Basel III Framework

attributes.name: fitch_rating_date
attributes.description: Date when the current Fitch issuer rating was assigned or last affirmed.

attributes.name: fitch_rating_outlook
attributes.description: Fitch's assessment of the potential direction of the issuer rating over a one to two-year period.

attributes.name: gics_sub_industry_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) Sub-Industry Code
attributes.description: Eight-digit GICS sub-industry code providing the most granular level of industry classification for specialized credit analysis.
attributes.references: MSCI GICS Methodology, S&P Global Industry Classification

attributes.name: internal_credit_rating
attributes.description: Bank's internal credit rating assigned through the Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approach. Used for economic capital allocation, pricing, and portfolio management when approved by regulators.
attributes.references: Basel III IRB Approach, Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: internal_lgd
attributes.description: Bank's estimate of the economic loss as a percentage of Exposure at Default if the issuer defaults. Expressed as percentage (e.g., 45.00 = 45%). Used for IRB capital and expected loss calculations.

attributes.name: internal_pd
attributes.description: Bank's estimate of the one-year probability of default for the issuer, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.015 = 1.5%). Core input for IRB capital calculations and CECL/IFRS 9 expected credit loss provisioning.
attributes.references: Basel III IRB Framework, IFRS 9, CECL Standard (ASC 326)

attributes.name: is_financial_institution
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the issuer is classified as a financial institution under Basel III. Determines interbank exposure treatment and contagion risk assessment.

attributes.name: is_investment_grade
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the issuer's credit rating meets investment grade threshold (BBB-/Baa3 or higher). Used for portfolio mandate compliance and risk appetite limits.
attributes.references: Investment Company Act Rule 2a-7, Basel III Framework

attributes.name: is_public_sector_entity
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the issuer is a public sector entity eligible for preferential risk weighting under Basel III Standardized Approach.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach, CRR Article 4(1)(8)

attributes.name: issuer_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the issuer entity. Inactive, merged, or bankrupt issuers require special handling for legacy securities and credit event processing.
attributes.references: ISDA Credit Events Definitions, Corporate Actions Standards

attributes.name: issuer_type
attributes.description: Classification of the issuer entity type. Determines applicable regulatory treatment, credit risk methodology, and capital requirements under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III Framework, BCBS Standards, IFRS 9

attributes.name: legal_name
attributes.description: The full legal name of the issuer as registered with the incorporation authority. This is the official name used in legal documents, securities filings, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: GLEIF LEI Standard, SEC Edgar Filing Requirements

attributes.name: moodys_issuer_rating
attributes.description: Current long-term issuer rating assigned by Moody's Investors Service. Used for credit risk assessment, portfolio limits, and regulatory capital calculations.
attributes.references: Moody's Rating Methodology, Basel III Framework

attributes.name: moodys_rating_date
attributes.description: Date when the current Moody's issuer rating was assigned or last affirmed.

attributes.name: moodys_rating_outlook
attributes.description: Moody's opinion on the likely direction of the issuer rating over the medium term.

attributes.name: primary_exchange_code
attributes.description: ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code (MIC) for the issuer's primary listing exchange. Used for market data sourcing and trading venue identification.

attributes.name: regulatory_classification
attributes.description: Basel III regulatory classification determining capital treatment, risk weighting methodology, and large exposure limits. Financial institutions receive different treatment than non-financial corporates.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach, CRR Article 4, Federal Reserve Regulation Q

attributes.name: sp_issuer_credit_rating
attributes.description: Current long-term issuer credit rating assigned by Standard & Poor's. Used for credit risk assessment, RWA calculation under Standardized Approach, and investment policy compliance.
attributes.references: S&P Global Ratings Methodology, Basel III Standardized Approach

attributes.name: sp_rating_date
attributes.description: Date when the current S&P issuer credit rating was assigned or last affirmed. Critical for determining rating staleness in credit risk models.

attributes.name: sp_rating_outlook
attributes.description: S&P's forward-looking opinion on the potential direction of the issuer credit rating over the intermediate term (typically 6-24 months).

attributes.name: ticker_symbol
attributes.description: Primary stock exchange ticker symbol for publicly traded issuers. Used for market data integration and equity price monitoring.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this issuer record was last modified. Critical for change data capture and downstream synchronization.

attributes.name: website_url
attributes.description: Official corporate website URL for the issuer. Used for investor relations access and ESG data sourcing.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation FD, Corporate Governance Standards

products.name: price
products.description: Immutable append-only time-series of all security price observations for all instruments, serving as the single source of truth for both current and historical pricing. Records bid, ask, mid, last trade, official closing, open, high, low, close, volume, VWAP, and adjusted close (for corporate actions). Stores price source (Bloomberg, Reuters/Refinitiv, exchange feed, broker quote, internal model), price type (market/model/indicative/official), pricing date and time, currency, price basis (clean/dirty for bonds), accrued interest, yield, spread to benchmark, price quality flag, and source system. Prices are never overwritten — corrections are appended with reason codes and supersession flags. Retains the complete historical price archive for all instruments across all time periods. Supports MTM valuation, NAV calculation, portfolio P&L attribution, IFRS 9 fair value measurement, backtesting, VaR historical simulation, performance attribution, regulatory stress testing (CCAR/DFAST), historical trend analysis, and time-series analytics.

attributes.name: price_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each price observation record in the immutable time-series.

attributes.name: benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.benchmark. Business justification: The price table contains spread_to_benchmark_bps — a spread measurement that is only meaningful relative to a specific benchmark (e.g., spread to US Treasury, spread to SOFR). Without a benchmark_id F

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Every price quote requires currency context for valuation and P&L calculation. Essential for multi-currency portfolio valuation, FX translation, and fair value hierarchy reporting under IFRS 13.

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Reference to the financial instrument being priced. Links to the security master for ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL, and instrument classification.

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: FRTB P&L attribution and stressed VaR require stressed mark-to-market prices computed under specific stress scenarios. A price record representing a stressed valuation must reference the scenario unde

attributes.name: superseded_by_price_id
attributes.description: Reference to the price_id of the corrected observation that supersedes this record. Null if this is the current valid observation.

attributes.name: accrued_interest
attributes.description: The interest accumulated on a fixed income security since the last coupon payment date. Used to calculate dirty price from clean price.

attributes.name: adjusted_close_price
attributes.description: The closing price adjusted for corporate actions (stock splits, dividends, rights issues) to maintain historical price continuity for performance analysis.

attributes.name: ask_price
attributes.description: The lowest price a seller is willing to accept for the security at the observation time. Used for liquidity analysis and bid-ask spread calculation.

attributes.name: basis
attributes.description: Indicates whether the price is clean (excluding accrued interest) or dirty (including accrued interest). Primarily applicable to fixed income securities.

attributes.name: bid_price
attributes.description: The highest price a buyer is willing to pay for the security at the observation time. Used for liquidity analysis and bid-ask spread calculation.

attributes.name: change_amount
attributes.description: The absolute change in price from the previous observation, calculated as current price minus prior price. Used for volatility analysis and market movement tracking.

attributes.name: change_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage change in price from the previous observation, calculated as ((current price - prior price) / prior price) * 100. Used for performance attribution and trend analysis.

attributes.name: confidence_score
attributes.description: A quantitative measure (0.0000 to 1.0000) representing the confidence or reliability of the price observation, derived from source quality, market liquidity, and validation checks.

attributes.name: correction_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code explaining why a price observation was corrected or superseded. Supports audit trail and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this price record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: A composite score (0.0000 to 1.0000) representing the overall quality of this price record based on completeness, timeliness, consistency, and validation checks.

attributes.name: fair_value_hierarchy_level
attributes.description: IFRS 13 / FASB ASC 820 fair value hierarchy classification: Level 1 (quoted prices in active markets), Level 2 (observable inputs), Level 3 (unobservable inputs).

attributes.name: high_price
attributes.description: The highest traded price of the security during the trading session or observation period.

attributes.name: is_superseded
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this price observation has been superseded by a subsequent correction or restatement. Supports immutable append-only architecture.

attributes.name: last_trade_price
attributes.description: The price at which the most recent trade was executed for this instrument. Represents actual market transaction price.

attributes.name: low_price
attributes.description: The lowest traded price of the security during the trading session or observation period.

attributes.name: mid_price
attributes.description: The midpoint between bid and ask prices, calculated as (bid + ask) / 2. Commonly used for fair value estimation and portfolio valuation.

attributes.name: notation
attributes.description: The format in which the price is expressed: decimal (e.g., 105.50), percentage (e.g., 98.75%), yield (e.g., 3.25%), basis points, or fractional (e.g., 32nds for US Treasuries).

attributes.name: observation_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this price record was captured and appended to the immutable time-series. Distinct from pricing_timestamp; supports data lineage and audit.

attributes.name: official_close_price
attributes.description: The official closing price published by the exchange or pricing authority at end of trading day. Used for Net Asset Value (NAV) calculation and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: open_price
attributes.description: The first traded price of the security at the start of the trading session.

attributes.name: price_source
attributes.description: The originating system or vendor that provided this price observation (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters/Refinitiv, exchange feed, broker quote, internal valuation model). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: bloomberg|reuters|refinitiv|exchange_feed|broker_quote|internal_model|vendor — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: price_status
attributes.description: The current status of pricing for this instrument: active (normal trading), suspended (temporarily halted), halted (trading stopped), delisted (removed from exchange), matured (instrument expired).

attributes.name: price_type
attributes.description: Classification of the price observation: market (actual traded price), model (derived from valuation model), indicative (non-binding quote), official (exchange-published), closing (end-of-day), opening (start-of-day).

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The business date for which this price observation is effective. Used for end-of-day valuations and historical analysis.

attributes.name: pricing_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this price observation was recorded or became effective. Critical for intraday Mark-to-Market (MTM) and trade execution analysis.

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of the reliability and timeliness of the price observation. Verified = confirmed by multiple sources; stale = outdated; estimated = model-derived; challenged = disputed or under review.

attributes.name: regulatory_price_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this price observation is used for regulatory reporting purposes (e.g., CCAR, DFAST, Basel III stress testing, IFRS 9 fair value measurement).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the upstream system that originated this price observation (e.g., Murex, Calypso, Bloomberg Terminal, internal pricing engine).

attributes.name: spread_to_benchmark_bps
attributes.description: The yield spread over a benchmark rate (e.g., LIBOR, SOFR, Treasury) expressed in basis points (BPS). Used for credit risk assessment and relative value analysis.

attributes.name: trading_session
attributes.description: Identifies the trading session during which the price observation was recorded (pre-market, regular hours, after-hours, overnight).

attributes.name: valuation_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to derive the price: quoted (exchange-traded), matrix (interpolated from comparable securities), model (internal valuation model), consensus (average of multiple sources), broker quote.

attributes.name: volume
attributes.description: The total number of units (shares, bonds, contracts) traded during the observation period. Used for liquidity assessment and market depth analysis.

attributes.name: vwap
attributes.description: The average price weighted by trading volume over the observation period. Used for execution quality assessment and algorithmic trading benchmarks.

attributes.name: yield_to_maturity
attributes.description: The total return anticipated on a bond if held until maturity, expressed as an annual percentage rate. Critical for fixed income valuation and portfolio analytics.

attributes.name: updated_by_user

products.name: benchmark
products.description: Master data for financial benchmarks, reference rates, and market indices with embedded daily rate observations and index constituent membership records. Covers SOFR, EURIBOR, SONIA, Fed Funds Rate, LIBOR (legacy), Treasury yield curves, credit spread indices (CDX, iTraxx), and equity indices (S&P 500, MSCI World, Bloomberg Barclays Aggregate). Captures benchmark name, administrator, IOSCO compliance status, publication frequency, currency, tenor, fallback rate provisions (LIBOR transition), and regulatory status. Includes daily published rate observations by tenor (overnight, 1M, 3M, 6M, 12M) with compounded rates, spread adjustments (for LIBOR-SOFR transition), and publication source. For indices, records constituent instruments with inclusion/exclusion dates, weights (market cap, par), rebalancing frequency, and rebalancing events. Supports floating rate coupon resets, swap valuation, FTP curve construction, passive portfolio management, index tracking, ETF basket construction, benchmark attribution, and ALM interest rate risk modeling.

products.name: yield_curve
products.description: Constructed yield curves and their constituent tenor-rate nodes used for instrument valuation, discounting, and risk measurement. Captures curve name, curve type (government, swap, credit spread, OIS), base currency, construction date, construction methodology (bootstrapping, interpolation method), and the complete set of tenor-rate nodes defining the curve shape. Each embedded node includes tenor label (1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 5Y, 10Y, 30Y), tenor in days, zero rate, par rate, forward rate, discount factor, and interpolation method applied between nodes. Supports bond pricing, derivative valuation (IRS, CDS), FTP curve construction, IFRS 9 ECL discount rate determination, DV01 sensitivity by tenor bucket, key rate duration analysis, and regulatory stress scenario application across the full term structure.

products.name: credit_rating

domains.name: trade
domains.description: Securities trading, order management, trade capture, execution, position management, P&L attribution, and post-trade processing for capital markets and trading book activities. Manages the full trade lifecycle from order entry through settlement, MTM valuation, trade confirmations, and FX/OTC derivative execution. Primary system of record aligned with Murex / Calypso.

products.name: order
products.description: Core master record for all trade orders entered into the Trading and Order Management System (Murex/Calypso). Supports parent/child order hierarchies for algorithmic and smart order routing. SSOT for trade order identity across capital markets.

attributes.description: Date on which the order automatically expires if not filled. Applicable for GTD (Good Till Date) orders. Null for Day, GTC, IOC, and FOK orders. System automatically cancels order at end of expiry date.

attributes.name: filled_quantity
attributes.description: Cumulative quantity executed to date. Updated as partial fills occur. When filled_quantity equals quantity, order status transitions to filled. Used to calculate remaining open quantity and order completion percentage.

attributes.name: is_discretionary

attributes.name: last_update_timestamp

attributes.name: limit_price

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of order execution instruction. Market orders execute immediately at best available price. Limit orders execute only at specified price or better. Stop orders trigger at specified price. IOC (Immediate or Cancel) and FOK (Fill or Kill) define time-in-force behavior.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of the security ordered. For equities, typically number of shares. For bonds, face value amount. For FX, base currency amount. For derivatives, number of contracts. Unit of measure depends on asset class and instrument type.

attributes.name: regulatory_trade_flag
attributes.description: Indicator for special regulatory treatment or reporting requirements. Examples include short sale indicator, large in scale (LIS), pre-trade transparency waiver, algorithmic trading flag. Used for regulatory reporting to FINRA, SEC, ESMA.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the order was rejected. Includes system validations (insufficient margin, invalid security), risk limit breaches, compliance blocks, or venue rejections. Null for non-rejected orders. Used for operational issue resolution and client communication.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the trade settles and securities and cash are exchanged. Calculated based on execution date and market convention (T+1 for US equities, T+2 for most securities). Critical for cash management and operational planning.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: Direction of the trade order. Buy increases position, sell decreases position. Short sell creates negative position. Buy to cover closes short position. Critical for position management and P&L calculation.

attributes.name: stop_price
attributes.description: Trigger price for stop and stop-limit orders. Order becomes active when market price reaches this level. Null for market and limit orders. Used for risk management and automated trading strategies.

attributes.name: time_in_force
attributes.description: Duration for which the order remains active. Day orders expire at market close. GTC (Good Till Cancelled) remains active until filled or cancelled. IOC (Immediate or Cancel) executes immediately or cancels. FOK (Fill or Kill) must fill completely or cancel. GTD (Good Till Date) expires on specified date.

products.name: capture
products.description: Authoritative trade booking record and single system of record in the trading platform (Murex/Calypso). Represents the confirmed, booked trade after execution, capturing trade date, value date, settlement date, notional amount, price/rate, accrued interest, trade currency, settlement currency, counterparty LEI, legal entity, trading book, and booking status. Supports all asset classes and product types including cash equities, bonds, IRS, CDS, FX spot/forward/swap/NDF, OTC options, equity swaps, and swaptions with product-type-specific attributes (e.g., UTI/USI for OTC derivatives, currency pair/forward points for FX, fixed/floating legs for swaps). Maintains full amendment and versioning history as lifecycle events on the trade record, including amendment type (economic amendment, administrative correction, novation, compression), amended fields with before/after values, amendment reason, approval workflow status, approver, amendment timestamp, and regulatory re-reporting flags for EMIR/Dodd-Frank/MiFID II. Each amendment creates a versioned snapshot preserving the complete audit trail. SSOT for the confirmed trade event, its full amendment audit trail, and all product types across capital markets.

products.name: trade_position
products.description: Real-time and end-of-day position record per trading book, instrument, and legal entity. Tracks long/short quantity, average cost, market value, unrealized P&L, realized P&L, accrued income, dirty/clean price, and Greek sensitivities (DV01, delta, gamma, vega, theta). Supports intraday position keeping, risk limit monitoring, regulatory capital calculations (FRTB), and serves as the base record for MTM revaluation and P&L attribution. Updated on each trade capture event, corporate action adjustment, and MTM revaluation cycle. Maintains position history for end-of-day snapshots enabling T-1 comparison and position break investigation.

attributes.name: pitch_date

attributes.name: pricing_date

attributes.name: rationale

attributes.name: consideration_type
attributes.description: Form of consideration offered in the transaction (e.g., cash, stock, mixed cash-and-stock, debt assumption, or earnout). Critical for M&A valuation, tax structuring, and shareholder approval requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transaction structure record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; FINRA Rule 4511 — Books and Records

attributes.name: cross_border_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction involves parties or assets in more than one country. Triggers additional regulatory, tax, and FX structuring considerations including CFIUS review for US transactions.
attributes.references: CFIUS (50 U.S.C. § 4565); EC Merger Regulation 139/2004; OECD BEPS

attributes.name: dcf_enterprise_value
attributes.description: Intrinsic enterprise value derived from the DCF valuation model underpinning the transaction structure. Represents the present value of projected free cash flows discounted at the WACC.
attributes.references: CFA Institute Valuation Standards; FASB ASC 820 — Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: deal_value_amount
attributes.description: Gross enterprise value or total deal consideration amount as agreed in the transaction structure. Represents the headline deal size used in pitch books, tombstones, and league table reporting.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 805; IFRS 3; SEC Regulation S-K Item 1.01

attributes.name: debt_assumed_amount
attributes.description: Total net debt assumed or refinanced as part of the transaction structure. Used in the enterprise-to-equity value bridge and leverage ratio calculations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 805; IFRS 3; Basel III — Leverage Ratio Framework

attributes.name: equity_value_amount
attributes.description: Equity value (market capitalisation or offer price times diluted shares) component of the transaction structure. Distinct from enterprise value; used in DCF valuation bridge and per-share consideration calculations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 805; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: exchange_ratio
attributes.description: Number of acquirer shares offered per target share in a stock-for-stock or mixed-consideration transaction. Null for cash-only deals. Used in merger proxy statements and SEC Form S-4 filings.
attributes.references: SEC Form S-4; FINRA Rule 5110; FASB ASC 805

attributes.name: expected_close_date
attributes.description: Anticipated date on which the transaction is expected to close and consideration is transferred. Used for deal pipeline forecasting and fee recognition scheduling.

attributes.name: fairness_opinion_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the board of directors requires a fairness opinion from an independent financial advisor to support the transaction. Typically required for related-party transactions and large public M&A.
attributes.references: Delaware Court of Chancery; SEC Schedule 14A; NYSE/NASDAQ Listing Rules

attributes.name: financing_mix_debt_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of total transaction financing sourced from debt instruments (senior secured, mezzanine, high-yield bonds). Used in leverage ratio analysis and pro forma capital structure modelling.
attributes.references: Basel III — Leverage Ratio; BCBS 270; LBO Structuring Standards

attributes.name: financing_mix_equity_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of total transaction financing sourced from equity (sponsor equity, management rollover, public equity issuance). Complements debt percentage to form the full financing mix.
attributes.references: Basel III — CET1; BCBS Capital Framework; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: lead_arranger_role
attributes.description: Role of the bank in this transaction structure (e.g., sole bookrunner, joint bookrunner, lead-left, financial advisor). Determines league table credit allocation and fee entitlement.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Dealogic / Bloomberg League Table Standards; LSTA

attributes.name: leverage_ratio
attributes.description: Pro forma leverage ratio expressed as total debt divided by EBITDA at transaction close. Key credit metric used by rating agencies, lenders, and regulators to assess transaction risk. Aligns with Basel III leverage ratio monitoring.
attributes.references: Basel III — Leverage Ratio Framework (BCBS 270); Moody's / S&P Rating Methodology

attributes.name: offer_premium_pct
attributes.description: Percentage premium offered over the target's unaffected share price (typically 30-day VWAP prior to announcement). Key M&A valuation metric used in fairness opinions and board presentations.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation 14D; FINRA Rule 5250; Delaware Court of Chancery Standards

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_bodies
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of regulatory bodies whose approval is required for this transaction (e.g., 'Fed, OCC, DOJ, EC'). Drives compliance workflow and deal timeline planning.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Regulation Y; OCC 12 CFR Part 5; HSR Act; EC Merger Regulation 139/2004

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction structure requires regulatory approval (e.g., antitrust clearance, banking regulator approval, securities regulator review) before closing.
attributes.references: HSR Act; EC Merger Regulation; Federal Reserve Regulation Y; OCC 12 CFR Part 5

attributes.name: shareholder_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction requires shareholder or bondholder approval (e.g., merger vote, rights issue prospectus approval). Triggers proxy statement and SEC Schedule 14A filing obligations.
attributes.references: SEC Schedule 14A; Delaware General Corporation Law; NYSE/NASDAQ Listing Rules

attributes.name: stock_consideration_amount
attributes.description: Equity (stock) portion of the total consideration, valued at the exchange ratio applied to the acquirer's share price. Used in share-for-share merger structuring and dilution analysis.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 805; IFRS 3; SEC Form S-4

attributes.name: structural_condition_type
attributes.description: Primary structural condition or protective mechanism embedded in the transaction agreement (e.g., MAC clause, financing condition, no-shop provision, breakup fee). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: material_adverse_change|regulatory_condition|financing_condition|no_shop|go_shop|breakup_fee|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISDA Master Agreement; Delaware Court of Chancery; SEC Regulation M-A

attributes.name: structure_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or working title for the transaction structure (e.g., 'Project Falcon — Leveraged Buyout Structure'). Treated as confidential pre-announcement deal information.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation FD; MAR (Market Abuse Regulation)

attributes.name: structure_reference_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to this transaction structure, used in pitch books, mandate letters, and regulatory filings (e.g., IB-2024-ACQX001).
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511 — Books and Records; SEC Regulation S-P

attributes.name: structure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the transaction structure from initial drafting through execution or termination. Drives workflow routing and deal pipeline reporting.
attributes.references: Internal Deal Governance Policy; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: structure_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investment banking transaction structure type. Drives applicable regulatory approvals, valuation methodology, and capital markets execution approach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: merger|acquisition|carve_out|spin_off|ipo|follow_on|rights_issue|bond_issuance|syndicated_loan|leveraged_buyout — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act 1933; SEC Exchange Act 1934; FINRA Rules

attributes.name: syndication_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the financing component of this transaction requires syndication to a group of lenders or underwriters (e.g., syndicated loan, bond roadshow). Triggers syndicate desk involvement.
attributes.references: Loan Syndications and Trading Association (LSTA) Standards; LMA Syndicated Loan Principles

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this completed transaction qualifies for inclusion in the bank's tombstone advertisement and league table submissions. Set to true upon successful close.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; Dealogic League Table Standards

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The principal real-world date on which the transaction structure was formally agreed, signed, or announced. Used as the primary business event date for deal timeline tracking and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: underwriting_fee_amount
attributes.description: Gross underwriting spread or fee for capital markets transactions (IPO, follow-on, bond issuance). Expressed as a total dollar amount; gross spread percentage is derived analytically.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110 — Underwriting Compensation; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transaction structure record was most recently modified. Used for change data capture, audit trail, and Silver Layer incremental processing.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; FINRA Rule 4511; GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity

attributes.name: wacc_rate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) Rate
attributes.description: Weighted average cost of capital rate used as the discount rate in the DCF valuation model for this transaction structure. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0850 = 8.50%).
attributes.references: CFA Institute Valuation Standards; FASB ASC 820

products.name: investment_valuation

Supports deal pricing, fiduciary duty compliance in public M&A, and investment committee approvals.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the valuation or fairness opinion was formally approved by the designated investment committee or approval authority. Marks the transition from in_review to approved status and is a key compliance milestone.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 14a-9; Internal Investment Banking Governance Policy

attributes.name: board_presentation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the valuation analysis or fairness opinion was formally presented to the client's board of directors. Required for fairness opinion compliance documentation and proxy statement disclosure. Distinct from the valuation date.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; Delaware General Corporation Law

attributes.name: conflict_check_status
attributes.description: Status of the investment bank's internal conflict of interest review for this valuation engagement. FINRA Rule 5150 requires disclosure of material relationships between the advisor and the parties to the transaction. Cleared indicates no material conflicts; conflict_identified requires disclosure or recusal.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 2010

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this valuation record was first created in the investment banking platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance record-keeping under SEC Rule 17a-4 and FINRA recordkeeping requirements.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: delivery_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the valuation analysis or fairness opinion letter was formally delivered to the client or their board of directors. Marks the transition to delivered status and is referenced in the engagement letter and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: enterprise_value_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the enterprise value range derived from the valuation analysis, expressed in the deal currency. The EV range reflects sensitivity analysis across key assumptions such as WACC and terminal growth rate.

attributes.name: enterprise_value_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the enterprise value range derived from the valuation analysis, expressed in the deal currency. Enterprise Value represents the total value of the business including debt and excluding cash. Used for deal pricing and fairness opinion conclusions.

attributes.name: equity_value_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied equity value range, calculated by deducting net debt from the enterprise value high. Used in conjunction with shares outstanding to derive implied per-share value ranges for board presentations and proxy filings.

attributes.name: equity_value_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied equity value range, calculated by deducting net debt from the enterprise value low. Represents the value attributable to equity holders and is used to derive implied share price ranges for M&A and IPO pricing.

attributes.name: ev_ebitda_multiple_high
attributes.business_glossary_term: Enterprise Value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) Multiple High
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied EV/EBITDA multiple derived from the valuation range. Together with the low multiple, defines the EV/EBITDA range used in board presentations, fairness opinion analyses, and investment committee materials.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; FINRA Rule 5150

attributes.name: ev_ebitda_multiple_low
attributes.business_glossary_term: Enterprise Value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) Multiple Low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied EV/EBITDA multiple derived from the valuation range, calculated as enterprise value low divided by the target company's EBITDA. Used to benchmark the valuation against comparable company trading multiples and precedent transaction multiples.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; FINRA Rule 5150

attributes.name: forecast_period_years
attributes.description: Number of years in the explicit cash flow forecast period used in the DCF or LBO model. Typically 5 to 10 years for investment banking valuations. Determines the horizon over which detailed financial projections are modeled before applying the terminal value.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: implied_share_price_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied per-share equity value derived from the equity value high divided by fully diluted shares outstanding. Together with the low, defines the implied share price range disclosed in fairness opinion proxy materials.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: implied_share_price_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied per-share equity value derived from the equity value low divided by fully diluted shares outstanding. Used in fairness opinion analyses to compare the implied price range against the proposed transaction consideration.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: is_fairness_opinion
attributes.description: Indicates whether this valuation record constitutes a formal fairness opinion (True) or an internal valuation analysis (False). Fairness opinions carry additional regulatory obligations under SEC Rule 14a-9 and FINRA Rule 5150, including board presentation and proxy disclosure requirements.

attributes.name: ltm_ebitda
attributes.description: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) for the last twelve months (LTM) period used as the primary financial metric in the valuation analysis. Denominator for EV/EBITDA multiple calculations and key input to DCF normalization.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; SEC Regulation S-X; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: material_relationship_disclosure
attributes.description: Narrative description of any material relationships between the investment bank and the parties to the transaction that must be disclosed in the fairness opinion letter or proxy statement, as required by FINRA Rule 5150. Includes prior advisory mandates, lending relationships, and equity holdings.

attributes.name: methodology
attributes.description: Primary valuation methodology applied in this analysis. Common investment banking methodologies include Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), Leveraged Buyout (LBO), Comparable Company Analysis, Precedent Transaction Analysis, Sum-of-Parts (SOTP), Net Asset Value (NAV), Dividend Discount Model (DDM), and Asset-Based valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DCF|LBO|comparable_company|precedent_transaction|sum_of_parts|NAV|dividend_discount|asset_based — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; IFRS 13; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: model_file_reference
attributes.description: Document management system reference or file path to the underlying financial model (Excel/Python workbook) supporting this valuation. Enables auditors and reviewers to trace the valuation conclusion back to the source model and assumptions.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 17a-4; Internal Model Risk Management Policy

attributes.name: net_debt
attributes.description: Total financial debt less cash and cash equivalents of the target company as of the valuation date, used to bridge from enterprise value to equity value. A negative net debt (net cash) position increases equity value relative to enterprise value.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; IFRS 13; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: opinion_conclusion
attributes.description: The formal conclusion of the fairness or solvency opinion as rendered by the investment bank. Applicable when is_fairness_opinion is True. The conclusion is disclosed in the proxy statement or offering document and is subject to SEC and FINRA scrutiny.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; Delaware General Corporation Law

attributes.name: opinion_type
attributes.description: Classification of the formal opinion rendered, applicable when is_fairness_opinion is True. Fairness opinions address whether consideration is fair from a financial point of view; solvency opinions address the target's ability to meet obligations post-transaction; valuation opinions provide a point estimate of value; adequacy opinions address whether consideration is adequate.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; Delaware General Corporation Law

attributes.name: pe_multiple_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied Price-to-Earnings (P/E) multiple derived from the equity value range. Together with the low multiple, defines the P/E range used in fairness opinion analyses and investment committee presentations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; SEC Rule 14a-9

attributes.name: pe_multiple_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied Price-to-Earnings (P/E) multiple derived from the equity value range divided by the target company's net income. Used as a cross-check valuation metric, particularly relevant for IPO pricing and public M&A transactions.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; SEC Rule 14a-9

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the valuation engagement, used in client deliverables, pitch books, and regulatory filings. Follows the format VAL-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: Internal Investment Banking Engagement Numbering Standard

attributes.name: shares_outstanding
attributes.description: Fully diluted shares outstanding of the target company as of the valuation date, including common shares, in-the-money options, warrants, and convertible securities on a treasury stock method basis. Used to derive implied per-share equity value.

attributes.name: target_company_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the company being valued or the target of the M&A transaction. Captured directly on the valuation record for reporting and audit purposes, as the target may not be an existing client in the customer master.

attributes.name: terminal_growth_rate
attributes.description: Perpetuity growth rate applied in the DCF terminal value calculation, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.025 for 2.5%). Represents the assumed long-term sustainable growth rate of the target company's free cash flows beyond the explicit forecast period.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investment banking transaction for which this valuation is being performed. attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; IASB IFRS 3

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording the most recent modification to this valuation record. Used for change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The as-of date on which the valuation analysis is anchored. All market data, financial projections, and comparable benchmarks are referenced as of this date. Critical for fairness opinion compliance and deal pricing.

attributes.name: valuation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the valuation record, tracking progression from initial draft through internal review, committee approval, client delivery, and potential supersession or withdrawal. attributes.name: version_number

attributes.name: wacc
attributes.description: Weighted Average Cost of Capital expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.085 for 8.5%) used as the discount rate in DCF valuation. Reflects the blended cost of equity and debt financing, adjusted for the target company's capital structure and risk profile.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; BCBS Basel III
