attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal IB Revenue Recognition Policy

attributes.name: bank_fee_share_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total fee retained by this bank after co-advisor fee sharing. Equals 100% minus co_advisor_fee_sharing_pct for simple two-party splits, or the bank's specific allocation in multi-party syndicates.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Syndicate Revenue Sharing Policy

attributes.name: break_fee_amount
attributes.description: The contractual fee payable to the bank if the deal is terminated by the client before completion. Compensates the bank for work performed and opportunity cost.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Mandate Agreement Template

attributes.name: co_advisor_fee_sharing_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total fee to be shared with co-advisors or syndicate members on the mandate. Used for fee split calculations and revenue attribution in multi-bank advisory or underwriting syndicates.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; IASB IFRS 15; Internal Syndicate Revenue Sharing Policy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this fee arrangement record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: deal_value_basis
attributes.description: The transaction or deal value (e.g., enterprise value, equity value, issuance proceeds) used as the basis for computing percentage-based fees. Critical for success fee and underwriting spread calculations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IASB IFRS 15

attributes.name: dispute_description
attributes.description: Description of the fee dispute raised by the client, including the disputed amount and grounds for dispute. Populated when payment_status is 'disputed'. Used for legal and collections management.
attributes.references: Internal Legal and Collections Policy; FINRA Dispute Resolution Rules

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee arrangement becomes legally binding and operative, typically aligned with the mandate agreement execution date.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: engagement_letter_ref
attributes.description: The document reference number of the signed engagement letter or mandate agreement that governs this fee arrangement. Used for legal and compliance audit trail.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Legal Document Management Policy

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee arrangement ceases to be operative. Nullable for open-ended arrangements. Tail fee provisions may extend beyond this date.

attributes.name: fee_amount
attributes.description: The gross base fee amount in the arrangement currency. For fixed-basis arrangements, this is the total contractual fee. For percentage-basis arrangements, this is the computed fee amount once the deal value is known. Used for P&L attribution and revenue recognition.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: fee_basis
attributes.description: The computational basis on which the fee is calculated. Fixed: flat dollar amount; Percentage: applied to transaction value or deal size; Tiered: percentage varies by deal size bracket; Blended: combination of fixed and percentage; Minimum Plus Percentage: floor amount plus variable component.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers; FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: fee_rate_bps
attributes.description: The fee rate expressed in basis points (BPS) applied to the transaction or deal value for percentage-basis fee arrangements. One basis point equals 0.01%. Used in underwriting spread and advisory fee calculations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; IASB IFRS 15; Internal IB Pricing Policy

attributes.name: fee_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fee by its commercial nature within the investment banking mandate. Retainer: periodic engagement fee; Success Fee: contingent on deal close; Underwriting Spread: difference between issue price and proceeds; Advisory Fee: M&A or capital markets advisory; Break Fee: payable on deal termination; Tail Fee: post-termination success fee within tail period.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 601; IASB IFRS 15

attributes.name: fee_waiver_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the business reason for waiving or reducing the contractual fee, required for management approval and audit trail when payment_status is 'waived'. Null when no waiver applies.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal IB Revenue Management Policy; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The accounts receivable invoice number issued to the client for fees due under this arrangement. Links to the AR module in the General Ledger system (Oracle Financials / SAP S4HANA) for payment tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal AR Policy; IASB IFRS 15

attributes.name: invoiced_amount
attributes.description: The total fee amount invoiced to the client under this arrangement. May differ from fee_amount due to adjustments, credits, or partial invoicing.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: The Line of Business (LOB) code identifying the investment banking division responsible for this fee arrangement (e.g., M&A Advisory, ECM, DCM, Leveraged Finance, Syndicated Lending).
attributes.references: Internal IB Revenue Management Policy; CCAR/DFAST LOB Segmentation

attributes.name: minimum_fee_amount
attributes.description: The contractual floor fee amount guaranteed to the bank regardless of deal size or outcome, applicable for tiered or minimum-plus-percentage fee basis arrangements.

attributes.name: payment_due_date
attributes.description: The contractual date by which the client must remit payment for the invoiced fee. Used for AR aging, collections management, and overdue fee tracking.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal AR Collections Policy

attributes.name: payment_received_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee payment was actually received from the client. Used for cash reconciliation, days-sales-outstanding (DSO) calculation, and revenue recognition confirmation.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: Current payment collection status for the fee arrangement. Pending: invoice issued, payment not yet due; Partially Paid: partial receipt; Paid: fully settled; Overdue: past due date; Waived: fee forgiven; Disputed: client has raised a dispute.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal AR Collections Policy; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: received_amount
attributes.description: The total fee amount actually received from the client as of the most recent payment event. Used for cash reconciliation, outstanding receivables tracking, and revenue recognition confirmation.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: reconciliation_reference
attributes.description: The payment or wire transfer reference number used to match the received fee payment to the invoice in the GL/AR system. Supports finance reconciliation and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Finance Reconciliation Policy; SWIFT Payment Standards

attributes.name: retainer_amount
attributes.description: The periodic retainer fee amount payable by the client during the engagement period, typically monthly or quarterly. May be credited against the success fee upon deal close.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Revenue Policy

attributes.name: retainer_creditable
attributes.description: Indicates whether retainer payments made during the engagement are creditable (offset) against the success fee upon deal completion. True = retainer amounts reduce the success fee payable.

attributes.name: retainer_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which retainer fee payments are due from the client during the engagement period.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal IB Engagement Letter Standards

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee revenue is recognized in the General Ledger per the applicable revenue recognition method (IFRS 15 / ASC 606). Critical for period-end financial close and P&L attribution.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_method
attributes.description: The accounting method applied to recognize revenue from this fee arrangement per IFRS 15 / ASC 606. Point in Time: recognized at deal close; Over Time: recognized ratably over engagement period; Milestone Based: recognized upon achievement of defined milestones; Contingent: deferred until contingency resolved.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: tail_period_months
attributes.description: The number of months following termination or expiry of the mandate during which the bank retains the right to a success fee if the client completes a transaction with a party introduced by the bank.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Mandate Agreement Template

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee arrangement is associated with a completed transaction eligible for tombstone publication (deal announcement). True = deal closed and fee earned; used for league table credit and marketing purposes.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Marketing Policy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this fee arrangement record was most recently modified. Audit trail field for change tracking, data lineage, and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Policy

Supports loan syndication desk operations and CLO/ABS structuring activities.

attributes.description: Reference to the borrower or obligor entity for whom the syndicated facility is being arranged. Core party reference for the syndication transaction.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.branch. Business justification: Syndication roadshows are physically hosted at specific branch offices. Branch-level roadshow tracking drives branch revenue credit, investor meeting logistics, and league table attribution. Investmen

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: Leveraged loan syndication commitments are stress-tested under CCAR/leveraged lending guidance scenarios to determine hold limits and selldown targets. Regulators require banks to demonstrate that syn

attributes.name: actual_selldown_amount
attributes.description: The amount actually distributed to third-party lenders at close of syndication. May differ from target_selldown_amount due to market conditions, pricing flex, or investor demand shortfall.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; IFRS 9

attributes.name: arrangement_fee_amount
attributes.description: The total arrangement fee earned by the bank for structuring and executing the syndication, expressed in deal currency. Recognized as fee income upon close per IFRS 15 / FASB ASC 606.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: Broad asset class of the syndicated instrument: leveraged_loan, investment_grade, Collateralized Loan Obligation (CLO), Asset-Backed Security (ABS), Mortgage-Backed Security (MBS), or project_finance. Drives regulatory capital treatment and investor eligibility.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; SEC Regulation AB; FRTB

attributes.name: bank_hold_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the total facility that the arranging bank intends to retain on its own balance sheet after syndication. Reflects the bank's final hold position and drives RWA and capital consumption calculations.
attributes.references: OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance; BCBS Basel III; LSTA Market Practice

attributes.name: bookrunner_role
attributes.description: The bank's role in the syndication as bookrunner or arranger: sole_bookrunner, joint_bookrunner, co_bookrunner, mandated_lead_arranger (MLA), or lead_arranger. Determines fee entitlement and decision-making authority in the syndicate.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: close_date
attributes.description: The date on which the syndication was formally closed and the credit agreement was executed with the final lender group. Corresponds to the effective date of the facility.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; FASB ASC 310

attributes.name: co_arranger_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of co-arranger bank names or BIC codes participating in the syndication alongside the bookrunner. Captures the arranger group composition for tombstone records, fee sharing, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; SWIFT BIC Standard

attributes.name: commitment_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline by which prospective lenders must submit their commitments during the bookbuilding phase. Drives the syndication desk's investor outreach timeline.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the syndication record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record origination and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; FASB ASC 310; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ Audit Trail

attributes.name: credit_rating_moodys
attributes.description: The Moody's Investors Service credit rating assigned to the syndicated facility or borrower at the time of syndication (e.g., Ba1, B2, Caa1). Used alongside S&P rating for dual-rating requirements in leveraged loan markets.
attributes.references: Moody's Investors Service; BCBS Basel III; SEC Rule 17g-5

attributes.name: credit_rating_sp
attributes.description: The Standard & Poor's credit rating assigned to the syndicated facility or the borrower at the time of syndication (e.g., BB+, B, CCC). Drives investor eligibility, pricing, and regulatory capital treatment.
attributes.references: S&P Global Ratings; BCBS Basel III IRB Approach; SEC Rule 17g-5

attributes.name: documentation_standard
attributes.description: The market documentation standard used for the syndicated loan agreement: LMA (Loan Market Association — EMEA), LSTA (Loan Syndication and Trading Association — US), APLMA (Asia Pacific), or bespoke. Governs transferability, voting thresholds, and secondary market conventions.
attributes.references: LMA Standard Documentation; LSTA Credit Agreement; APLMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: esg_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the syndicated facility is structured as an ESG-linked loan or sustainability-linked loan (SLL), where pricing is tied to the borrower's ESG performance targets. Supports green finance reporting and investor ESG mandates.
attributes.references: LMA Green Loan Principles; LMA Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles; ICMA Green Bond Principles

attributes.name: flex_amount_bps
attributes.description: The magnitude of the pricing flex applied, expressed in basis points. Positive value indicates widening; negative value indicates tightening. Captures the delta between initial price talk and final pricing.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: launch_date
attributes.description: The date on which the syndication was formally launched to the market, i.e., when the information memorandum and term sheet were distributed to prospective lenders.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: league_table_credit
attributes.description: Determines how this syndication is credited in investment banking league tables: full_credit (sole bookrunner), pro_rata (shared among joint bookrunners), or no_credit (co-arranger only). Drives competitive ranking and business development reporting.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Standards; LSTA

attributes.name: lender_count
attributes.description: The total number of lenders in the final syndicate at close. Indicates syndication breadth and diversification of the lender group; used in post-deal analytics and tombstone records.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: leveraged_loan_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the syndicated facility meets the OCC/Fed/FDIC definition of a leveraged loan (typically total debt/EBITDA > 4x or borrower rated below investment grade). Triggers enhanced regulatory scrutiny and reporting under interagency leveraged lending guidance.
attributes.references: OCC/Fed/FDIC Leveraged Lending Guidance (2013); BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 13-3

attributes.name: mandate_date
attributes.description: The date on which the borrower formally awarded the syndication mandate to the arranging bank(s). Marks the start of the syndication process and triggers fee accrual.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: oid_bps
attributes.description: The original issue discount expressed in basis points, representing the upfront discount to par at which the loan is issued to lenders. Common in leveraged loan syndications; impacts lender yield and borrower all-in cost.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; IRS OID Rules (IRC §1272); FASB ASC 835-30

attributes.name: oversubscription_amount
attributes.description: The amount by which investor commitments exceeded the target syndication amount during bookbuilding. A positive value indicates strong market demand; used for pricing flex decisions and greenshoe allocation.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The date on which final pricing (spread, OID, fees) was determined and communicated to lenders. Marks the transition from bookbuilding to allocation in the syndication lifecycle.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; FINRA TRACE

attributes.name: pricing_flex_type
attributes.description: Indicates the direction of pricing flex applied during bookbuilding: tightened (spread reduced due to oversubscription), held (no change), flexed_wider (spread increased due to weak demand), oid_added, oid_increased, or structure_changed. Key indicator of market reception.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: purpose_code
attributes.description: The stated purpose of the syndicated facility: acquisition_finance, leveraged_buyout (LBO), refinancing, general_corporate, capital_expenditure (capex), or working_capital. Used for regulatory classification, OCC leveraged lending identification, and portfolio analytics.
attributes.references: OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance (2013); BCBS Basel III; LSTA Market Practice

attributes.name: reference
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to the syndication transaction, used in deal communications, tombstones, and regulatory filings. Corresponds to the deal reference in Loan IQ.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: spread_bps
attributes.description: The credit spread over the reference rate expressed in basis points (BPS) at which the syndicated facility is priced. Core pricing parameter for lender economics and secondary market trading.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; ISDA

attributes.name: syndication_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the syndication process: mandate_awarded (bank selected as arranger), launched (syndication formally opened to market), bookbuilding (collecting lender commitments), priced (spread and terms finalized), closed (facility fully allocated), withdrawn (deal pulled from market), failed (insufficient demand). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mandate_awarded|launched|bookbuilding|priced|closed|withdrawn|failed|post_close — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: syndication_type
attributes.description: Classification of the syndication structure: primary_syndication (initial distribution to lender group), secondary_sell_down (post-close transfer of hold), club_deal (small bilateral group), best_efforts (no underwriting commitment), underwritten (bank commits full amount). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: primary_syndication|secondary_sell_down|club_deal|best_efforts|underwritten|participation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: target_selldown_amount
attributes.description: The target amount the bank aims to distribute to third-party lenders through the syndication process. Equals total_facility_amount minus bank_hold_amount at deal inception; may be revised during bookbuilding.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: tenor_months
attributes.description: The contractual tenor of the syndicated facility expressed in months from the close date to final maturity. Key parameter for duration risk, regulatory capital, and investor suitability assessment.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; BCBS Basel III

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bank has received borrower consent to publicize this transaction in a tombstone announcement. Required before any deal announcement in pitch books, league tables, or press releases.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; SEC Regulation FD

attributes.name: total_facility_amount
attributes.description: Gross size of the syndicated credit facility or capital markets transaction in the deal currency. Represents the full commitment amount before any sell-down or hold reduction.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; IFRS 9; FASB ASC 310

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent update to the syndication record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver layer ETL pipeline and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ Audit Trail; Databricks Delta Lake CDC

attributes.name: upfront_fee_bps
attributes.description: The upfront participation fee paid to lenders expressed in basis points of their commitment. Incentivizes early commitment during bookbuilding and is a key component of lender all-in yield.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; FASB ASC 310-20

Tracks the bank's risk exposure during the underwriting period.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: Regulatory jurisdiction determines prospectus requirements (SEC S-1, EU Prospectus Regulation), underwriting agreement enforceability, and securities law compliance framework.

attributes.name: risk_limit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_limit. Business justification: Underwriting commitments (underwritten_amount, commitment_type) are directly constrained by underwriting risk limits (single-issuer, sector, country). The underwriting desk operates within hard risk l

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: Underwriting commitments carry rwa_amount and capital charges calculated under specific stress scenarios (CCAR, DFAST). Regulatory capital adequacy assessment of underwriting books requires linking ea

attributes.name: agreement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal underwriting agreement between the bank (and co-underwriters) and the issuer was executed. This is the legally binding contract governing the terms of the underwriting commitment.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Section 11; FINRA Rule 5110; ISDA Framework

attributes.name: bank_allocation_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total offering size allocated to this bank as its underwriting commitment share within the syndicate. Determines the bank's proportional fee entitlement and risk exposure.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Syndicate Management Standard

attributes.name: book_runner_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bank is acting as a bookrunner (lead or joint) for this offering, responsible for managing the order book during the book-building process. True if the bank has bookrunner responsibilities; False for co-manager or selling group roles.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Syndicate Role Classification Standard

attributes.name: commitment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the bank formally committed to underwrite the offering, typically coinciding with the signing of the mandate letter or underwriting agreement. Marks the start of the bank's underwriting risk exposure period.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Deal Lifecycle Standard

attributes.name: commitment_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this underwriting commitment, used in mandate letters, syndicate agreements, and regulatory filings. Format: LOB-UW-YYYY-NNNNNN.

attributes.name: commitment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the underwriting commitment. Mandated: bank has received the mandate; Active: commitment is live during the offering period; Priced: pricing has been set; Closed: transaction has settled; Withdrawn: issuer withdrew the offering; Terminated: commitment cancelled prior to pricing.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Lifecycle Management Standard

attributes.name: commitment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the underwriting commitment structure. Firm commitment means the bank purchases all securities and resells them; best efforts means the bank sells as much as possible without guaranteeing the full amount; standby is used in rights offerings; all-or-none requires full subscription or cancellation; mini-max sets a minimum threshold.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this underwriting commitment record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS BCBS 239 Data Governance; Internal Audit Trail Standard

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SEC registration statement became effective, permitting the public sale of securities. For Rule 144A transactions, this is the date the offering memorandum was finalized.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Section 8; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: expected_fee_revenue
attributes.description: The bank's expected gross fee revenue from this underwriting commitment, calculated as the bank's allocated underwriting spread applied to its committed underwriting amount. Used for revenue forecasting, deal profitability analysis, and RAROC (Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital) calculations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; IFRS 15; Internal FTP (Funds Transfer Pricing) Standard

attributes.name: fee_bps
attributes.description: The portion of the underwriting spread allocated as the underwriting fee, expressed in basis points. Compensates syndicate members for bearing the underwriting risk during the offering period.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: greenshoe_option_amount
attributes.description: The maximum additional amount (in base currency) that the underwriters may purchase from the issuer under the over-allotment (greenshoe) option, typically up to 15% of the base offering size. Exercised to stabilize the aftermarket price. Named after the Green Shoe Manufacturing Company, the first company to use this mechanism.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-7; Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: greenshoe_option_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an over-allotment (greenshoe) option has been granted to the underwriters in this transaction. True if a greenshoe option exists; False if no over-allotment option is included.

attributes.name: league_table_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transaction qualifies for inclusion in investment banking league table rankings (e.g., Bloomberg, Dealogic, Thomson Reuters). Transactions may be excluded due to size thresholds, role limitations, or issuer type restrictions.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Standards; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: lock_up_period_days
attributes.description: The number of days following the offering during which existing shareholders and insiders are contractually prohibited from selling their shares. Typically 90 or 180 days for IPOs. Relevant for aftermarket risk management and secondary trading restrictions.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; NYSE/NASDAQ Listing Standards

attributes.name: management_fee_bps
attributes.description: The portion of the underwriting spread allocated as the management fee, expressed in basis points. Compensates the lead manager(s) for structuring, due diligence, and transaction management responsibilities.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: mandate_letter_date
attributes.description: The date on which the issuer formally awarded the underwriting mandate to the bank via a signed mandate letter. Precedes the commitment date and marks the formal engagement of the bank as underwriter.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Investment Banking Mandate Management Standard

attributes.name: offering_price
attributes.description: The final public offering price per unit (share or bond face value) at which securities are sold to investors. For equity, expressed as price per share; for debt, expressed as a percentage of par value. Determined at pricing date.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 501; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: offering_size
attributes.description: The total gross proceeds of the offering at the offering price, representing the full transaction size including any greenshoe option if exercised. Distinct from underwritten_amount which reflects only the bank's committed portion.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 501; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the final offering price and size are determined through the book-building process. Marks the end of the primary underwriting risk period for firm commitment transactions as the spread is locked in.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: prospectus_type
attributes.description: The type of SEC registration statement or offering document filed for this transaction. S-1 is the standard IPO registration; S-3 is for seasoned issuers; F-1 is for foreign private issuers; 424B is the final prospectus; offering memorandum is used for 144A/Reg S private placements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: s1|f1|s3|s11|424b|offering_memorandum|prospectus_supplement|base_prospectus — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; SEC Forms S-1, S-3, F-1; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: roadshow_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the investor roadshow commenced for this offering. The roadshow is the marketing period during which management presents to institutional investors prior to pricing.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Deal Lifecycle Standard

attributes.name: rwa_amount
attributes.description: The Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) amount attributable to this underwriting commitment, calculated per Basel III standardized or internal ratings-based (IRB) approach. Drives capital charge allocation and CET1 (Common Equity Tier 1) consumption reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; OCC Capital Adequacy Standards; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST

attributes.name: sec_file_number
attributes.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) file number assigned to the registration statement for this offering (e.g., 333-XXXXXX for Securities Act registrations). Used for regulatory tracking and EDGAR cross-referencing.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Section 8; SEC EDGAR Filing System

attributes.name: selling_concession_bps
attributes.description: The portion of the underwriting spread allocated as the selling concession, expressed in basis points. Paid to dealers and selling group members for distributing securities to end investors.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the securities are delivered to investors and proceeds are remitted to the issuer. Typically T+1 for US equity offerings and T+2 or T+3 for debt. Marks the completion of the underwriting commitment.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 15c6-1 (T+1 Settlement); FINRA Rule 11860; DTCC Settlement Standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this underwriting commitment record originated (e.g., MUREX or CALYPSO for trading/deal capture, DEALOGIC for deal tracking, LOAN_IQ for syndicated lending mandates). Required for data lineage and ETL reconciliation.
attributes.references: BCBS BCBS 239 Data Aggregation and Reporting Principles; Internal Data Lineage Standard

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: The native primary key or record identifier of this underwriting commitment in the originating operational system of record (e.g., Murex deal ID, Calypso transaction ID, Dealogic deal reference). Enables bi-directional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source system.
attributes.references: BCBS BCBS 239 Data Aggregation and Reporting Principles; Internal Data Lineage Standard

attributes.name: spread_bps
attributes.description: The total underwriting spread expressed in basis points (BPS), representing the difference between the price paid to the issuer and the public offering price. This is the primary revenue metric for the underwriting commitment and is split among syndicate members per the fee allocation agreement.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: stabilization_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bank is acting as stabilizing manager for this offering, authorized to conduct price stabilization transactions in the aftermarket to support the offering price. True if the bank has stabilization responsibilities.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-7; EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) Article 5; FCA Stabilisation Rules

attributes.name: syndicate_role
attributes.description: The bank's role within the underwriting syndicate. Lead bookrunner has primary responsibility for book building and allocation; joint bookrunner shares that responsibility; co-manager has a smaller participation; selling group members distribute but do not underwrite. Determines fee economics and regulatory obligations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IOSCO Principles for Secondary Markets

attributes.name: tombstone_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tombstone advertisement has been published for this completed transaction. Tombstones are formal announcements of completed capital markets transactions and serve as marketing credentials for the bank's league table rankings.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Investment Banking Marketing Standard

attributes.name: underwritten_amount
attributes.description: The gross principal amount (in base currency) that the bank has committed to underwrite for this transaction. For firm commitment deals, this represents the bank's maximum financial exposure prior to distribution. Key input for RWA (Risk-Weighted Assets) and capital charge calculations under Basel III.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this underwriting commitment record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL (Extract Transform Load) processing.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS BCBS 239 Data Governance; Internal Audit Trail Standard

products.name: investor_order
products.description: Transactional record capturing individual investor orders received during the bookbuilding process for ECM and DCM transactions. Records investor name, order type (strike, limit, step), order size, price limit, order date and time, order status (active, filled, cancelled), allocation received, and investor tier classification. Enables bookrunner to manage the order book and determine final pricing and allocation.
products.reference: Bookbuilding Order / Investor Indication of Interest

attributes.name: investor_order_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each investor order record in the bookbuilding order book. Primary key for the investor_order data product.

attributes.name: coverage_assignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the sales professional or relationship manager who solicited or managed this investor order on behalf of the bookrunner. Used for sales credit attribution, commission calculation, and investor relationship tracking.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4512; SEC Rule 17a-3; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent capital markets transaction (ECM or DCM deal) for which this investor order was submitted during the bookbuilding process.

attributes.name: digital_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.digital_channel. Business justification: MiFID II and SEC best-execution rules require recording the specific digital channel (electronic order book, client portal, API) through which an investor order was placed. The existing branch_id cove

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.fund_class. Business justification: Investor orders in fund share offerings are placed for a specific share class, determining applicable fees, minimum investment thresholds, and investor eligibility. Allocation and settlement processes

Business justification: Investor order settlement date calculations and allocation timestamp validation require holiday calendar reference. Banking capital markets operations use holiday calendars to determine valid settleme

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.instrument. Business justification: Investor orders in offerings are for specific instruments. Required for order book management, allocation algorithms, settlement file generation, and post-IPO position reconciliation. Complements exis

attributes.name: investor_geography_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.country. Business justification: Investor geography required for Reg S/144A eligibility determination, geographic allocation analysis, and cross-border securities offering compliance.

attributes.name: kyc_review_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.kyc_review. Business justification: Investor orders in capital markets require KYC clearance before allocation. investment_investor_order.kyc_status is a denormalization of kyc_review status. Direct FK enables compliance to confirm whic

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investment bank or syndicate member acting as bookrunner who received and recorded this investor order. In syndicated deals, multiple bookrunners may collect orders from different investor segments.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: order_currency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Investor order book management, allocation sizing, and settlement require a proper currency reference for the order denomination. Banking capital markets teams use currency reference for cross-currenc

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the institutional or retail investor entity that submitted this order. Links to the investor master record for KYC and AML compliance purposes.

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.profit_center. Business justification: Investor order allocations generate distribution revenue attributed to profit centers in capital markets. Required for revenue attribution reporting and measuring capital markets desk profitability by

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sanctions_screening_event. Business justification: Every investor order must be screened against OFAC/sanctions lists before allocation. Mandatory compliance control for capital markets offerings. Screening event records match status, disposition, and

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.session. Business justification: Electronically placed investor orders must be linked to the authenticated session for audit trail, fraud detection, and regulatory compliance (MiFID II order record-keeping). Banking operations requir

attributes.name: settlement_account_deposit_account_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Settlement Account Deposit Account Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to account.deposit_account. Business justification: Capital markets investor orders settle cash through specific deposit accounts. Settlement operations require validated account linkage for payment processing, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting

attributes.name: allocation_amount
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the allocation received by the investor, calculated as allocation_size multiplied by allocation_price. Represents the investor's financial commitment to the transaction. Used for settlement, fee calculation, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: allocation_price
attributes.description: The final deal price per share or per unit at which the investor's allocation was confirmed. Typically the IPO offer price or bond issue price. Used for settlement and P&L attribution.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: allocation_size
attributes.description: The number of shares or face value amount actually allocated to the investor following the bookrunner's allocation decision at deal pricing. Zero if the order was not filled. Compared against order_size to determine fill ratio.
attributes.references: IOSCO Principles for IPO Bookbuilding; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation M

attributes.name: allocation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the allocation decision was communicated to the investor following deal pricing. Marks the transition from bookbuilding to allocation phase. Used for settlement timeline tracking (T+1, T+2).
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation M; T+1 Settlement Rule

attributes.name: cancellation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the investor cancelled or withdrew the order from the book. Null if the order was not cancelled. Used for demand attrition analysis and bookbuilding audit trail.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-3; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this investor order record was first captured and persisted in the order management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes. May differ from order_timestamp if there is a processing lag.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-3; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: custodian_name
attributes.description: Name of the custodian bank or prime broker responsible for holding the allocated securities on behalf of the investor. Used for settlement instruction routing and corporate trust/custody services coordination.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17f-1; FINRA Rule 4311; Corporate Trust and Custody Services standards

attributes.name: demand_multiple
attributes.description: Ratio of the investor's order size to the investor's expected or target allocation, indicating the degree of oversubscription at the individual investor level. Used by the bookrunner to assess investor conviction and calibrate allocation decisions.

attributes.name: greenshoe_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this investor order is eligible to be filled from the overallotment (greenshoe) option, allowing the bookrunner to allocate up to 15% additional shares beyond the base offering size to cover excess demand.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M Rule 104; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Rule 10b-7

attributes.name: investor_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the investor or institution placing the order. Used for order book management, allocation decisions, and regulatory reporting. May represent an institutional fund, asset manager, or individual investor.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4512; SEC Rule 17a-3; GDPR Article 4; FATCA

attributes.name: investor_tier
attributes.description: Classification of the investor by tier, which influences allocation priority and deal economics. 'anchor' investors commit pre-IPO with lock-up; 'cornerstone' investors receive guaranteed allocations; 'institutional' covers qualified institutional buyers (QIBs); 'retail' covers individual investors; 'strategic' covers corporate or government investors with strategic interest.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; SEC Rule 144A; FINRA Rule 5110; Hong Kong SFC Listing Rules

attributes.name: investor_type
attributes.description: Categorization of the investor by institutional type. Drives regulatory treatment, allocation policy, and suitability assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: asset_manager|hedge_fund|pension_fund|sovereign_wealth|insurance|bank|family_office|retail|corporate|endowment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: MiFID II Article 4; SEC Rule 144A; FINRA Rule 4512; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: is_anchor_investor
attributes.description: Indicates whether this investor has been designated as an anchor investor for the transaction, committing to a pre-IPO allocation with a lock-up period. Anchor investors receive guaranteed allocations in exchange for early commitment and price support.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; Hong Kong SFC Listing Rules; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: is_covered_short
attributes.description: Indicates whether the investor's order includes a covered short sale component, typically associated with the greenshoe/overallotment option exercise. Relevant for stabilization and price support analysis post-IPO.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M Rule 104; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Rule 10b-21

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this investor order record, including status changes, order amendments, or allocation updates. Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-3; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: lock_up_period_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days the investor is contractually restricted from selling the allocated securities following the deal closing date. Applicable primarily to anchor and cornerstone investors. Zero or null if no lock-up applies.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 144; FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: order_amendment_count
attributes.description: Number of times the investor has amended this order during the bookbuilding period (e.g., size increases, price limit changes). Tracks investor conviction and demand evolution. Used for bookbuilding analytics and investor behavior analysis.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-3; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: order_channel
attributes.description: The channel through which the investor submitted the order to the bookrunner. 'electronic' covers order management system portals; 'voice' covers telephone orders; 'email' covers written email instructions; 'roadshow' covers orders placed during investor roadshow meetings; 'bloomberg' covers Bloomberg order management system submissions.
attributes.references: MiFID II Article 25; FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-3

attributes.name: order_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the investor submitted the order during the bookbuilding period. Used for day-level reporting and analysis of demand build-up over the bookbuilding timeline.

attributes.name: order_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing additional instructions, conditions, or commentary provided by the investor or the sales coverage team regarding this order. May include special allocation requests, investment rationale, or bookrunner observations.

attributes.name: order_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this investor order, used for communication between the bookrunner and the investor during the bookbuilding process. Corresponds to the order ticket number in the Trading and Order Management System (e.g., Murex/Calypso).

attributes.name: order_size
attributes.description: The total number of shares (for ECM) or face value amount (for DCM) that the investor has requested in this order. Represents the gross demand submitted by the investor before any allocation decision.
attributes.references: IOSCO Principles for IPO Bookbuilding; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the investor order within the bookbuilding process. 'active' indicates the order is live in the book; 'filled' indicates full allocation received; 'partially_filled' indicates partial allocation; 'cancelled' indicates investor withdrew the order; 'expired' indicates the order lapsed at book close.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Regulation M; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: order_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone) at which the investor submitted the order to the bookrunner. This is the principal real-world business event timestamp for the order, critical for time-priority allocation and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-3; FINRA Rule 4511; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investor order by pricing instruction: 'strike' (accept final IPO/deal price), 'limit' (maximum price the investor will pay), 'step' (tiered quantity at different price levels), 'capped' (maximum size cap), 'uncapped' (no size restriction). Drives bookrunner pricing and allocation logic.
attributes.references: IOSCO Principles for IPO Bookbuilding; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: price_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the price limit is expressed. May differ from order_currency in cross-border transactions where the security is priced in a different currency than the order denomination.

attributes.name: price_limit
attributes.description: The maximum price per share or per unit that the investor is willing to pay for a limit order. Null for strike orders where the investor accepts the final deal price. Used by the bookrunner to determine price sensitivity and construct the demand curve.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation M

attributes.name: regulatory_category
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the investor order under applicable securities law. 'qib' = Qualified Institutional Buyer under SEC Rule 144A; 'reg_s' = offshore investor under SEC Regulation S; 'retail' = retail investor under applicable prospectus rules; 'employee' = employee share plan participant; 'directed' = directed share program recipient.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 144A; SEC Regulation S; FINRA Rule 5110; EU Prospectus Regulation

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system of record from which this investor order was originated or captured. Supports data lineage and ETL audit trail in the Databricks Silver Layer. Typical sources include Murex, Calypso, iPreo (bookbuilding platform), Dealogic, Bloomberg OMS, or manual entry.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS 239 Data Lineage Principles

attributes.name: step_price_1
attributes.description: First price level for a step order, representing the price at which the investor commits to the quantity specified in step_size_1. Applicable only for order_type = 'step'. Null for non-step orders.

attributes.name: step_price_2
attributes.description: Second price level for a step order, representing the price at which the investor commits to the quantity specified in step_size_2. Null for non-step orders or step orders with only one tier.

attributes.name: step_size_1
attributes.description: Quantity (shares or face value) the investor will take at step_price_1 in a step order. Represents the first tier of a tiered demand schedule. Null for non-step orders.

attributes.name: step_size_2
attributes.description: Quantity (shares or face value) the investor will take at step_price_2 in a step order. Represents the second tier of a tiered demand schedule. Null for non-step orders.

attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Capital Framework

attributes.name: maturity_date
attributes.description: Date on which the principal amount of a debt security is due for repayment to bondholders. Applicable to bond and note offerings (investment grade, high yield, convertible). Null for equity offerings.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 470 (Debt); IFRS 9; SEC Regulation S-K Item 202; FINRA TRACE

attributes.name: offer_price
attributes.description: Final price per share or per unit at which securities are offered to investors, set at pricing date. For debt offerings, expressed as a percentage of par value (e.g., 99.50). Central pricing fact for the ECM/DCM transaction.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 424(b); FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Principles for Primary Markets

attributes.name: offering_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned by the investment banking division to uniquely identify this offering across deal management, regulatory filing, and syndication systems (e.g., ECM-2024-00123).

attributes.name: offering_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the capital markets offering, tracking progression from deal pipeline through regulatory filing, investor roadshow, pricing, and final closing or withdrawal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pipeline|mandated|filed|roadshow|priced|closed|withdrawn|postponed — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; OCC Guidance on Capital Markets Activities

attributes.name: overallotment_amount
attributes.description: Additional securities amount available under the overallotment (greenshoe) option, typically up to 15% of the base offering size. Exercisable by the stabilizing manager to cover excess demand and support post-listing price stability.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-7; FINRA Rule 5110; EU Prospectus Regulation

attributes.name: price_range_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the indicative price range communicated to investors during the roadshow and bookbuilding process, prior to final pricing. Used in preliminary prospectus and investor marketing materials.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 424(b); EU Prospectus Regulation; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: price_range_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the indicative price range communicated to investors during the roadshow and bookbuilding process, prior to final pricing. Used in preliminary prospectus and investor marketing materials.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 424(b); EU Prospectus Regulation; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The principal business event date on which the offering price was formally set and agreed between the issuer, underwriters, and investors. Represents the key transaction event timestamp for ECM/DCM deal records.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 424(b); FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Principles for Secondary Markets

attributes.name: rating_agency
attributes.description: Name of the Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization (NRSRO) that assigned the credit rating to this debt offering. NR indicates the offering is not rated. Null for equity offerings.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17g-5; Dodd-Frank Act Section 939A; IOSCO Code of Conduct for Credit Rating Agencies

attributes.name: reg_s_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the offering is eligible for distribution to non-US investors under SEC Regulation S (offshore transactions), enabling international tranche distribution without full SEC registration.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S; Securities Act of 1933; FATCA; CRS (OECD)

attributes.name: roadshow_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investor roadshow and bookbuilding process concluded, immediately preceding the pricing date. Used to measure roadshow duration and investor engagement analytics.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 134; FINRA Rule 5110; EU Prospectus Regulation

attributes.name: roadshow_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investor roadshow and bookbuilding process commenced. Marks the beginning of formal investor marketing and demand generation for the offering.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 134; FINRA Rule 5110; EU Prospectus Regulation

attributes.name: rule_144a_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the offering qualifies for resale to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) under SEC Rule 144A, enabling a private placement tranche alongside or instead of a registered public offering.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 144A; Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which securities are delivered to investors and proceeds are remitted to the issuer, typically T+1 or T+2 from pricing date per applicable exchange and regulatory settlement conventions.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 15c6-1 (T+1 Settlement); DTCC Settlement Standards; ISDA Settlement Guidelines

attributes.name: shares_offered
attributes.description: Total number of shares or units offered in the transaction (base offering, excluding overallotment). Applicable to equity offerings (IPO, follow-on, rights issue). For debt offerings, represents face value units.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 501; FINRA Rule 5110; NYSE/NASDAQ Listing Standards

attributes.name: size_amount
attributes.description: Total gross proceeds targeted to be raised in the offering, expressed in the offering currency. Represents the base deal size before any overallotment (greenshoe) exercise. Core monetary fact for ECM/DCM transaction records.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 501; FINRA Rule 5110; Basel III Capital Adequacy Framework

attributes.name: stabilization_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the stabilizing manager is authorized to conduct post-listing price stabilization activities (e.g., greenshoe exercise, open market purchases) to support the offering price in the secondary market.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-7; EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) Article 5; FCA MAR Stabilisation Rules

attributes.name: syndicate_size
attributes.description: Total number of investment banks participating in the underwriting syndicate for this offering, including bookrunners, co-managers, and selling group members. Indicates deal complexity and distribution breadth.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: tombstone_published_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the tombstone announcement (deal announcement advertisement) has been published following successful closing of the offering. Tombstones serve as the official public record of completed capital markets transactions.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Rule 134; Investment Banking Industry Practice

attributes.name: total_proceeds_amount
attributes.description: Actual total gross proceeds raised at closing, including any overallotment option exercised. Represents the final deal size and is the primary monetary outcome metric for the offering.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 424(b); FINRA Rule 5110; FASB ASC 505 (Equity)

attributes.name: underwriting_discount_bps
attributes.description: Gross underwriting spread expressed in basis points (BPS) as a percentage of total offering proceeds. Represents the total fee paid to the underwriting syndicate, covering management fee, underwriting fee, and selling concession.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508; IOSCO Principles for Primary Markets

attributes.name: underwriting_fee_amount
attributes.description: Absolute monetary value of the gross underwriting fee payable to the underwriting syndicate, derived from the underwriting discount applied to total proceeds. Key revenue metric for investment banking P&L attribution.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508; FASB ASC 340-10 (Revenue Recognition)

attributes.name: use_of_proceeds
attributes.description: Narrative description of how the issuer intends to deploy the capital raised from the offering (e.g., debt repayment, capital expenditure, working capital, acquisitions). Required disclosure in the prospectus under SEC Regulation S-K Item 504.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 504; EU Prospectus Regulation Annex I; FCA Listing Rules

domains.name: wealth
domains.description: Wealth management and private banking including portfolio construction, asset allocation, AUM tracking, NAV calculation, client reporting, rebalancing, and investment policy statements. Manages high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth client relationships and suitability assessments. Primary system of record aligned with SimCorp Dimension / BlackRock Aladdin.
domains.references: SEC Investment Advisers Act, FINRA Suitability

products.name: managed_portfolio
products.description: Core master entity representing a discretionary or advisory investment portfolio managed on behalf of a high-net-worth (HNW) or ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) client. Captures portfolio strategy, benchmark assignment, base currency, AUM, inception date, mandate type (discretionary/advisory), risk profile, investment horizon, fee structure reference, and portfolio status (active/suspended/closed/terminated). Links to client_mandate for contractual terms, investment_policy_statement for investment strategy and pre-mandate proposals, model_portfolio for template allocation and asset allocation targets, and custodian_account for safekeeping. Primary system of record aligned with SimCorp Dimension / BlackRock Aladdin portfolio master.

attributes.name: fee_rate

attributes.name: fee_schedule_code

attributes.name: fee_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fee being charged. attributes.name: fee_waiver_amount

attributes.name: flat_fee_amount

attributes.name: gl_posting_reference

attributes.name: gross_fee_amount

attributes.name: high_water_mark

attributes.name: invoice_date

attributes.name: invoice_reference_number

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: negotiated_discount_percentage

attributes.name: net_fee_amount

attributes.name: payment_date

attributes.name: payment_due_date

attributes.name: performance_hurdle_rate

attributes.name: regulatory_disclosure_flag

attributes.name: version

attributes.name: payment_method

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_date
