domains.name: risk
domains.description: Enterprise-wide risk measurement and management covering market risk (VaR, CVA), credit risk (RWA, ECL), operational risk (SMA), and liquidity risk (LCR, NSFR). Supports CCAR, DFAST stress testing, RAROC, KRI monitoring, IRB models, PD/LGD/EAD aggregation, and risk appetite framework. Primary system of record aligned with SAS Risk Management / Moodys RiskAuthority.
domains.references: Basel III, BCBS 239, Dodd-Frank, FRTB, CCAR, DFAST

products.name: factor
products.description: Master registry of all enterprise risk factors used in quantitative risk models. Captures market risk drivers (interest rate curves, FX rates, equity indices, commodity prices, credit spreads), credit risk parameters (PD, LGD, EAD), and operational risk indicators. Each factor has a unique identifier, factor type, asset class, tenor/maturity, data source, calibration methodology, historical time series reference, and regulatory classification under Basel III/FRTB. Serves as the canonical SSOT for risk factor definitions and model linkage.
products.reference: Basel III Risk Factor / FRTB Risk Factor

attributes.name: factor_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each risk factor record in the enterprise risk factor master registry. Serves as the primary key for all downstream model linkages and risk calculations.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) — FRTB SA/IMA Risk Factor Standards

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code associated with the risk factor (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP'). For FX risk factors, this is the base currency. For interest rate factors, this is the currency of the underlying rate curve. Null for non-currency-denominated factors such as equity indices.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; BCBS FRTB FX Risk Class Definition

attributes.name: holiday_calendar_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.holiday_calendar. Business justification: FRTB RFET requires 250 trading-day observation windows; risk factor observation counts depend on the applicable market holiday calendar. Linking factor to holiday_calendar enables accurate trading-day

attributes.name: jurisdiction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: FRTB and Basel IV risk factor classification is jurisdiction-specific — EU CRR3 and US Basel III endgame have different modellability and bucketing rules. Linking factors to jurisdiction enables juris

attributes.name: rate_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.rate_benchmark. Business justification: FRTB risk factor assignment and VaR model calibration require linking risk factors to their underlying benchmark rate (SOFR, EURIBOR, etc.). Market risk quants use this to map rate sensitivity factors

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: Risk factors are shocked under stress scenarios. The risk_factor table has stress_period_start_date, stress_period_end_date, ccar_scenario_flag — these link to stress_scenario definitions. N:1 relatio

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: Broad asset class to which the risk factor belongs under the FRTB framework. Determines the applicable sensitivity-based method (SBM) bucket, risk weight, and correlation parameters for regulatory capital computation.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — Asset Class Definitions; OCC Market Risk Rule

attributes.name: calibration_method
attributes.description: Statistical methodology used to calibrate the risk factor's shock distribution and volatility parameters for VaR, stressed VaR, and ECL models. Governs model validation requirements and regulatory approval under IRB and IMA frameworks.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 Model Risk Management; BCBS FRTB IMA — Calibration Standards; IFRS 9 ECL Model Requirements

attributes.name: ccar_scenario_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR) Scenario Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk factor is included in the Federal Reserve's CCAR/DFAST stress testing scenario framework. True for factors that are shocked in supervisory adverse and severely adverse scenarios. Governs inclusion in stress testing data submissions to the Federal Reserve.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Instructions; Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing (DFAST) Requirements; Fed SR 15-18

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk factor record was first created in the enterprise risk factor registry. Provides the audit trail entry point for data lineage and regulatory examination purposes. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: BCBS 239 — Data Lineage and Audit Trail; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: credit_quality
attributes.description: Credit quality classification of the reference entity or issuer underlying a credit spread risk factor. Determines the applicable FRTB risk weight and correlation parameters. 'investment_grade' corresponds to IG-rated issuers (BBB- and above); 'sub_investment_grade' to HY/NR issuers.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — CSR Risk Weights by Credit Quality; Basel III IRB Credit Quality Steps; S&P/Moody's Rating Scales

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this risk factor definition became effective and was approved for use in production risk models. Marks the start of the factor's active lifecycle in the enterprise model inventory.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 Model Lifecycle Management; BCBS 239 Data Governance

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this risk factor definition expires or is scheduled for retirement from production models. Null for open-ended factors with no planned expiry. Used for model lifecycle management and proactive replacement planning (e.g., LIBOR cessation dates).
attributes.references: SR 11-7 Model Lifecycle Management; FSOC LIBOR Transition Timeline

attributes.name: factor_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code identifying the risk factor across systems (e.g., 'IR_USD_SOFR_3M', 'FX_EURUSD', 'EQ_SPX'). Used as the canonical business identifier in model configurations, regulatory submissions, and cross-system references.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Risk Factor Eligibility Test (RFEТ); SAS Risk Management Factor Registry

attributes.name: factor_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description of the risk factor, including its economic interpretation, model usage context, known limitations, and any special handling instructions. Supports model documentation requirements under SR 11-7 and provides context for risk analysts and model validators.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 — Model Documentation Standards; BCBS 239 Metadata Requirements

attributes.name: factor_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the risk factor as used in business communications, model documentation, and regulatory reports (e.g., 'USD SOFR 3-Month Swap Rate', 'EUR/USD Spot FX Rate', 'S&P 500 Equity Index').
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325; ISDA Risk Factor Taxonomy

attributes.name: factor_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the risk factor in the enterprise model inventory. 'active' factors are used in live production models; 'deprecated' factors are retained for historical audit; 'under_review' factors are undergoing model validation or regulatory review.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 — Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management; OCC Model Risk Guidance

attributes.name: factor_type
attributes.description: Primary classification of the risk factor by its economic nature. Drives model selection, regulatory capital treatment, and VaR/CVA calculation methodology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: interest_rate|fx_rate|equity|commodity|credit_spread|volatility|inflation|real_estate|pd|lgd|ead — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — Risk Factor Classification; Basel III Market Risk Framework

attributes.name: frtb_bucket
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) Bucket
attributes.description: FRTB Sensitivity-Based Method (SBM) bucket assignment for this risk factor as defined in BCBS FRTB Article 325. Determines the applicable risk weight and intra-bucket/inter-bucket correlation parameters for regulatory capital computation (e.g., 'GIRR_Bucket_1', 'CSR_non_sec_Bucket_3', 'EQ_Bucket_7').
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — SBM Bucket Definitions; EBA ITS on FRTB SA

attributes.name: geography
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country or region code indicating the geographic jurisdiction of the risk factor (e.g., 'USA' for US rates, 'GBR' for UK gilts, 'EMU' for Eurozone). Used for geographic concentration analysis, country risk reporting, and regulatory capital bucketing.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; BCBS FRTB — Country Risk Buckets; EBA Country Risk Reporting

attributes.name: holding_period_days
attributes.description: Regulatory or internal holding period in calendar days used for VaR and Expected Shortfall (ES) calculations for this risk factor (e.g., 10 days for market risk under Basel, 1 day for internal daily VaR). Determines the time horizon over which potential losses are measured.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Liquidity Horizon Requirements; Basel III Market Risk — 10-Day VaR; ISDA SIMM

attributes.name: ifrs9_ecl_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Financial Reporting Standard 9 (IFRS 9) Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk factor is used as a macroeconomic variable or credit parameter in IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss (ECL) models. True for factors such as GDP growth, unemployment rate, PD term structures, and LGD curves used in forward-looking ECL projections.
attributes.references: IFRS 9 — Impairment and ECL Model Requirements; IASB IFRS 9 Application Guidance; CECL ASC 326

attributes.name: is_proxy_factor
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk factor is used as a proxy for another illiquid or unobservable factor. True when the factor substitutes for a non-modellable risk factor (NMRF) in model calculations. Proxy relationships require additional model validation documentation under SR 11-7.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Non-Modellable Risk Factor (NMRF) Treatment; SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

attributes.name: last_observation_date
attributes.description: Most recent date on which a real market price observation was recorded for this risk factor. Used in RFET assessment to verify that the factor has sufficient recent observations to qualify as modellable under FRTB IMA. Critical for daily data quality monitoring.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Risk Factor Eligibility Test (RFET); BCBS 239 Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: last_validation_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent independent model validation review for this risk factor's calibration and methodology. Required under SR 11-7 to ensure ongoing model fitness. Triggers re-validation workflow when the elapsed period exceeds the validation frequency threshold.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 — Independent Model Validation Requirements; OCC Model Risk Guidance 2011-12

attributes.name: liquidity_horizon_days
attributes.description: FRTB-prescribed liquidity horizon in days assigned to this risk factor, reflecting the time required to exit or hedge the risk position in stressed market conditions (e.g., 10, 20, 40, 60, or 120 days per FRTB asset class). Used in ES scaling for IMA capital calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — Liquidity Horizon Categories; EBA ITS on FRTB IMA Liquidity Horizons

attributes.name: market_data_source
attributes.description: Name of the primary market data vendor or internal source from which this risk factor's time series is sourced (e.g., 'Bloomberg', 'Refinitiv', 'ICE Data Services', 'Federal Reserve H.15', 'Internal Pricing Model'). Governs data lineage and RFEТ (Risk Factor Eligibility Test) compliance under FRTB IMA.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Risk Factor Eligibility Test (RFET); BCBS 239 Data Lineage Requirements

attributes.name: market_data_ticker
attributes.description: Vendor-specific ticker or field identifier used to retrieve this risk factor's market data from the designated source system (e.g., Bloomberg ticker 'USGG10YR Index', Refinitiv RIC '.SPX'). Enables automated data feed mapping and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Bloomberg Data License Standards; Refinitiv Data Model; BCBS 239 RDARR

attributes.name: next_validation_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next independent model validation review of this risk factor. Computed based on the validation frequency policy (e.g., annual for Tier 1 models, biennial for Tier 2). Drives the model validation calendar and resource planning.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 — Model Validation Frequency; OCC Model Risk Guidance 2011-12

attributes.name: observation_window_days
attributes.description: Length of the historical data observation window in calendar days used for calibrating this risk factor's shock distribution (e.g., 250 days for 1-year VaR, 1260 days for 5-year stressed VaR). Governs the backtesting and RFET assessment period.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Historical Observation Period Requirements; SR 11-7 Model Validation

attributes.name: proxy_factor_code
attributes.description: Factor code of the observable proxy risk factor used when is_proxy_factor is True. Documents the substitution relationship for model validation, audit, and NMRF capital add-on calculations. Null when the factor is directly observable.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — NMRF Proxy Methodology; SR 11-7 Model Documentation Requirements

attributes.name: regulatory_classification
attributes.description: FRTB IMA classification of the risk factor as 'modellable' (RFET passed — sufficient real price observations) or 'non_modellable' (NMRF — requires stressed scenario capital add-on). Directly impacts IMA capital calculation and must be reported to regulators. 'not_applicable' for SA-only factors.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — Risk Factor Eligibility Test (RFET); EBA ITS on FRTB IMA; OCC Market Risk Rule

attributes.name: rfet_observation_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk Factor Eligibility Test (RFET) Observation Count
attributes.description: Number of real price observations recorded for this risk factor over the RFET assessment period (typically 12 months). A minimum of 24 observations (or 100 for the alternative test) is required for the factor to be classified as modellable under FRTB IMA. Populated by the market data quality process.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — RFET Minimum Observation Thresholds; EBA ITS on FRTB IMA

attributes.name: risk_class
attributes.description: Enterprise risk classification indicating which risk management pillar this factor belongs to: market risk (VaR, CVA), credit risk (PD/LGD/EAD, ECL, RWA), operational risk (SMA), or liquidity risk (LCR, NSFR). Governs routing to the appropriate risk engine and regulatory reporting stream.
attributes.references: Basel III Pillar 1 — Market, Credit, and Operational Risk; BCBS 239 RDARR

attributes.name: sector
attributes.description: Industry sector classification of the risk factor's underlying issuer or reference entity (e.g., 'financials', 'energy', 'technology', 'sovereign', 'covered_bond'). Applies primarily to credit spread and equity risk factors. Aligns with FRTB SBM sector buckets for correlation and risk weight assignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: financials|energy|technology|sovereign|covered_bond|consumer_discretionary|industrials|utilities|real_estate|materials — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — CSR and Equity Sector Buckets; GICS Sector Classification

attributes.name: shock_type
attributes.description: Convention used to express risk factor shocks in sensitivity and scenario analyses: 'absolute' (additive shift in units), 'relative' (percentage change), 'log_return' (log-normal return), or 'basis_point' (1bp = 0.0001 shift for rates). Determines how sensitivities (delta, vega) are computed and reported.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Sensitivity Calculation Standards; ISDA SIMM Shock Conventions

attributes.name: stress_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the identified historical stress period used for stressed VaR and FRTB stressed ES calibration. Together with stress_period_start_date, defines the calibration window that produces the most adverse 12-month stressed scenario for this risk factor.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Stressed ES Calibration; Basel II.5 Stressed VaR Requirements; Fed DFAST Stress Scenarios

attributes.name: stress_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the identified historical stress period used for stressed VaR (sVaR) and FRTB stressed ES calibration for this risk factor. Must correspond to a period of significant financial stress relevant to the factor's asset class (e.g., 2008-09-01 for the Global Financial Crisis).
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Stressed ES Calibration; Basel II.5 Stressed VaR Requirements; Fed DFAST Stress Scenarios

attributes.name: sub_risk_class
attributes.description: Granular sub-classification within the primary risk class (e.g., 'general_interest_rate_risk', 'specific_risk', 'counterparty_credit_risk', 'settlement_risk', 'concentration_risk'). Used for detailed regulatory reporting and internal risk appetite segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: general_interest_rate_risk|specific_risk|counterparty_credit_risk|settlement_risk|concentration_risk|basis_risk|vega_risk|curvature_risk — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Sensitivity-Based Method Sub-Risk Classes; EBA ITS on Market Risk

attributes.name: tenor
attributes.description: Maturity or tenor of the risk factor along the yield curve or term structure (e.g., '3M', '1Y', '10Y'). Applicable to interest rate, credit spread, and volatility surface factors. Null for spot FX rates and equity spot factors. Aligns with FRTB prescribed tenor vertices for delta sensitivity calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB Article 325 — Prescribed Tenor Vertices; ISDA SIMM Tenor Buckets

attributes.name: tenor_days
attributes.description: Numeric representation of the risk factor tenor expressed in calendar days (e.g., 90 for 3M, 365 for 1Y). Enables precise interpolation between tenor vertices in risk model calculations and facilitates sorting and bucketing of term structure factors.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Interpolation Standards; ISDA Risk Factor Tenor Conventions

attributes.name: time_series_code
attributes.description: Reference to the historical time series record in the market data repository that stores the daily observations for this risk factor. Enables direct linkage from the factor definition to its underlying data for backtesting, calibration, and RFET assessment.
attributes.references: BCBS 239 — Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting; BCBS FRTB Data Requirements

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit in which the risk factor value is expressed (e.g., 'percent', 'basis_points', 'USD_per_barrel', 'index_points', 'USD_per_troy_oz'). Essential for correct interpretation of factor values, shock magnitudes, and sensitivity calculations across heterogeneous risk factor types.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Risk Factor Value Conventions; ISDA Risk Factor Taxonomy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this risk factor record. Tracks changes to factor definitions, calibration parameters, or regulatory classifications. Essential for change management audit trails and regulatory examination readiness.
attributes.references: BCBS 239 — Data Lineage and Audit Trail; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: var_confidence_level
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level used when computing Value at Risk (VaR) for this risk factor (e.g., 0.9900 for 99%, 0.9750 for 97.5% ES under FRTB). Stored as a decimal fraction. Governs the tail risk threshold for internal risk limits and regulatory capital calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Expected Shortfall at 97.5% Confidence; Basel II.5 VaR at 99% Confidence; Fed CCAR Stress Testing

attributes.name: var_contribution_pct
attributes.description: Percentage contribution of this risk factor to the total portfolio VaR as of the last calculation date. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0523 = 5.23%). Used for risk attribution reporting, limit monitoring, and identification of dominant risk drivers in the trading book.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB — Risk Attribution; Basel III Market Risk Capital; Internal Risk Appetite Framework

products.name: appetite
products.description: Enterprise risk appetite framework defining quantitative and qualitative thresholds, tolerances, and limits across all risk categories (credit, market, liquidity, operational). Captures board-approved risk appetite statements, metric definitions, breach escalation rules, and linkage to ALCO/CCAR governance. Serves as the authoritative source for enterprise-wide risk tolerance boundaries.

attributes.name: appetite_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each risk appetite statement or threshold record within the enterprise risk appetite framework.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Risk Appetite Framework; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: jurisdiction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: Risk appetite statements are set per regulatory jurisdiction — DFAST appetite differs from PRA/EBA requirements. Board-approved appetite documents reference specific regulatory frameworks tied to juri

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Board-approved risk appetite frameworks are entity-specific; SREP and ICAAP regulatory submissions require appetite statements attributed to specific legal entities. The plain column legal_entity on a

attributes.name: superseded_by_appetite_id
attributes.description: Reference to the risk_appetite_id of the newer version that supersedes this record when approval_status is 'superseded'. Enables forward-chaining of the version history for audit and regulatory review purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; BCBS Corporate Governance; FSB Risk Appetite Framework

attributes.name: appetite_level
attributes.description: Qualitative board-approved appetite level indicating the degree of risk the institution is willing to accept in pursuit of its strategic objectives. Ranges from low (minimal risk tolerance) to high (aggressive risk-taking within regulatory bounds).
attributes.references: FSB Principles for Sound Risk Appetite Frameworks; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the governing body formally approved this risk appetite statement. Critical for audit trail, SOX compliance, and regulatory examination documentation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles; Fed SR 12-17

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the risk appetite statement within the governance approval workflow. Tracks progression from initial drafting through board approval to eventual supersession or retirement.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: breach_escalation_level
attributes.description: Defines the escalation tier that must be notified upon breach of this appetite threshold. Establishes the governance response chain from management-level notification through CRO to Board Risk Committee escalation.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles; Fed SR 11-7

attributes.name: breach_response_timeframe_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of calendar days within which a formal remediation plan must be submitted to the designated escalation body following a breach of this appetite threshold.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; OCC Risk Governance Handbook; Fed SR 11-7

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk appetite record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX, BCBS 239 data lineage standards, and regulatory examination documentation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; BCBS 239 Data Quality Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether the appetite threshold represents a minimum floor (e.g., CET1 ratio must be at least X%), a maximum ceiling (e.g., NPL ratio must not exceed Y%), a target value, or a permissible range.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; Fed CCAR; IFRS 9

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this risk appetite statement becomes binding and operative across the institution. Aligns with the board approval cycle, typically annual or triggered by material risk profile changes.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Supervisory Review Process; Fed CCAR Annual Cycle

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this risk appetite statement ceases to be operative and must be reviewed, renewed, or superseded. Null for open-ended statements that remain in force until explicitly retired.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Annual Review Requirements

attributes.name: governance_body
attributes.description: The governing body that approved this risk appetite statement (e.g., Board of Directors, Board Risk Committee, ALCO, Executive Risk Committee). Establishes the authority level and escalation chain for breach management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: board|board_risk_committee|alco|executive_risk_committee|credit_committee|audit_committee|cro_office — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FSB Corporate Governance Principles; BCBS Corporate Governance Guidelines; Fed SR 12-17

attributes.name: is_board_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk appetite statement has received formal Board of Directors or Board Risk Committee approval (True) or is still in draft/management-approved status (False). Required for regulatory examination and SOX attestation.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles; Fed SR 12-17

attributes.name: is_quantitative
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk appetite statement is expressed as a quantitative metric with a numeric threshold (True) or as a qualitative statement without a numeric bound (False). Qualitative statements include zero-tolerance policies for regulatory violations or reputational risk.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Risk Appetite Guidance

attributes.name: is_regulatory_minimum
attributes.description: Indicates whether this appetite threshold is set at or derived from a regulatory minimum requirement (True) or represents an internally-set management buffer above the regulatory floor (False). Critical for distinguishing regulatory compliance floors from internal risk management buffers.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Minimum Capital Requirements; Fed CCAR Minimum Ratios; OCC Capital Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: kri_code
attributes.description: Reference code linking this risk appetite statement to the corresponding Key Risk Indicator (KRI) in the enterprise GRC system. Enables automated monitoring of appetite utilization against real-time KRI readings from SAS Risk Management / Moodys RiskAuthority.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk SMA; OCC KRI Guidance; Fed SR 11-7

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which this risk appetite statement was most recently reviewed and reaffirmed or amended by the governing body. Provides audit evidence of ongoing governance oversight.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; SOX Section 302; BCBS Corporate Governance

attributes.name: limit_value
attributes.description: Hard operational limit assigned to a specific business line, desk, or portfolio that must not be exceeded. Derived from and subordinate to the enterprise-level appetite threshold. Used in daily risk limit monitoring within the Trading and Order Management System (Murex/Calypso).
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB; FINRA Rule 4370; Fed SR 11-7; ISDA CSA

attributes.name: line_of_business
attributes.description: The specific Line of Business (LOB) to which this appetite statement applies (e.g., 'Commercial Lending', 'Investment Banking', 'Retail Banking', 'Securities Trading', 'Wealth Management'). Null if the statement applies enterprise-wide.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk SMA; Fed CCAR LOB Segmentation; FINRA LOB Reporting

attributes.name: metric_definition
attributes.description: Formal definition of how the risk metric is calculated or assessed, including the numerator, denominator, observation period, and data sources. Ensures consistent measurement across business lines and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; IFRS 9; FASB CECL; Fed SR 11-7

attributes.name: metric_name
attributes.description: Name of the quantitative or qualitative metric used to measure risk against this appetite statement (e.g., 'CET1 Ratio', 'VaR 99% 10-day', 'LCR', 'NSFR', 'NPL Ratio', 'ECL Coverage Ratio').
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; Fed CCAR/DFAST; IFRS 9; FASB CECL

attributes.name: metric_unit
attributes.description: Unit in which the risk metric is expressed (e.g., percentage for CET1 ratio, currency_usd for VaR dollar amount, basis_points for credit spread limits, days for LCR horizon). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: percentage|ratio|currency_usd|currency_local|basis_points|count|score|days — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; ISDA Definitions; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formal review of this risk appetite statement by the designated governance body. Derived from the last review date and review frequency; used to drive governance workflow alerts.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Annual Review Requirements

attributes.name: qualitative_statement
attributes.description: Full text of the board-approved qualitative risk appetite statement for non-quantifiable risk types (e.g., 'The Bank has zero tolerance for breaches of AML/BSA regulations' or 'The Bank will not engage in activities that materially damage its reputation'). Populated when is_quantitative is False.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; FinCEN BSA/AML Requirements; BCBS Corporate Governance

attributes.name: range_lower_bound
attributes.description: Lower boundary of the acceptable risk range when direction is 'range'. Applicable for metrics such as NIM targets or LCR operating ranges where both a floor and ceiling are defined.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR/NSFR Standards; ALCO Policy Framework

attributes.name: range_upper_bound
attributes.description: Upper boundary of the acceptable risk range when direction is 'range'. Used alongside range_lower_bound to define the full operating corridor for metrics managed within a band.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR/NSFR Standards; ALCO Policy Framework

attributes.name: raroc_hurdle_rate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC) Hurdle Rate
attributes.description: Minimum Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC) threshold that business activities must meet to be consistent with this risk appetite statement. Used in capital allocation decisions and new product approval processes.
attributes.references: BCBS Pillar 2 ICAAP; Fed CCAR Capital Planning; RAROC Methodology

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: Mandated frequency at which this risk appetite statement must be formally reviewed and reaffirmed by the governing body. Drives the governance calendar for ALCO and Board Risk Committee scheduling.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Supervisory Review; OCC Risk Governance Handbook

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: Primary risk category to which this appetite statement applies. Aligns with the enterprise risk taxonomy: credit, market, liquidity, operational, reputational, or strategic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: credit|market|liquidity|operational|reputational|strategic|compliance|model|concentration — promote to reference product if taxonomy expands]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Framework; OCC Risk Governance Handbook; FSB Risk Appetite Framework

attributes.name: risk_sub_category
attributes.description: Granular sub-classification within the primary risk category (e.g., 'Counterparty Credit Risk', 'Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB)', 'Intraday Liquidity Risk', 'Cyber Operational Risk'). Supports drill-down analytics in CCAR and DFAST reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS IRRBB Standards; FRTB Framework; OCC Operational Risk Guidance

attributes.name: rwa_limit
attributes.description: Maximum Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) allocated to the applicable business line or portfolio under this appetite statement. Expressed in the institution's reporting currency. Supports capital adequacy management under Basel III Standardized Approach (SA) and Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) Approach.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III RWA Framework; Fed CCAR; OCC Capital Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this risk appetite record originates or is maintained (e.g., SAS_RM for SAS Risk Management, MOODYS_RA for Moodys RiskAuthority, AXIOMSL for AxiomSL regulatory reporting platform, MANUAL for board-documented statements).
attributes.references: Enterprise Data Governance Policy; BCBS Data Quality Principles (BCBS 239)

attributes.name: statement_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the risk appetite statement, used in board documentation, ALCO packs, and regulatory submissions (e.g., RA-CREDIT-2024-001).
attributes.references: BCBS Risk Appetite Framework; Federal Reserve CCAR Guidance

attributes.name: statement_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the risk appetite statement as approved by the Board Risk Committee (e.g., 'Maximum Credit Risk Concentration — Single Obligor').
attributes.references: BCBS Risk Appetite Framework; FSB Principles for Sound Risk Appetite Frameworks

attributes.name: stress_scenario_applicability
attributes.description: Indicates which stress testing scenario(s) this appetite threshold applies to: baseline (normal conditions), adverse (moderate stress), severely adverse (severe stress), or all scenarios. Directly maps to CCAR/DFAST scenario definitions.
attributes.references: Fed CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing Guidance; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: threshold
attributes.description: Board-approved quantitative value representing the maximum level of risk the institution is willing to accept under normal operating conditions. For example, a CET1 ratio floor of 11.5% or a VaR limit of USD 50 million.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III CET1 Requirements; Fed CCAR Minimum Capital Ratios; IFRS 9 ECL

attributes.name: tolerance_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable deviation from the risk appetite threshold before mandatory escalation is triggered. Represents the outer boundary of acceptable risk exposure (e.g., CET1 floor of 10.5% as the tolerance boundary below the 11.5% appetite).
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; BCBS Supervisory Review Process (Pillar 2); OCC Risk Governance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this risk appetite record in the data platform. Used for change data capture, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance per BCBS 239 data governance standards.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; BCBS 239 Data Quality Principles; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this risk appetite statement, incremented each time the statement is formally amended and re-approved. Enables version history tracking and audit trail for regulatory examination.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles; Fed SR 12-17

attributes.name: warning_threshold
attributes.description: Early-warning trigger level set between the appetite threshold and tolerance threshold. Breaching this level initiates management-level monitoring and pre-emptive action before the tolerance boundary is reached. Supports KRI monitoring frameworks.
attributes.references: FSB Risk Appetite Framework; Fed SR 11-7; OCC KRI Guidance

products.name: risk_limit
products.description: Operational risk limit registry, utilization tracking, and breach management record. Captures approved exposure limits by risk type (credit, market, liquidity, concentration), counterparty, portfolio, desk, LOB, and geography. Includes limit amount, currency, effective/expiry dates, approval authority, utilization basis, and breach action rules. Records limit breach events including breach date/time, limit type, breached threshold, actual value, excess amount, severity classification, responsible desk/LOB, escalation chain, remediation actions, and resolution status. Supports real-time limit monitoring, breach governance, and regulatory capital constraint management under Basel III/FRTB.

attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each risk limit record in the operational risk limit registry. Primary key for the risk_limit data product. Entity role: MASTER_AGREEMENT — represents a binding, approved exposure constraint with its own lifecycle, approval authority, and utilization tracking.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) — Basel III Framework; BCBS FRTB

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.product_type. Business justification: Risk limits are set by product type for regulatory capital management — e.g., maximum exposure to leveraged loans, structured credit concentration limits. Product-type-scoped limits are standard in cr

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.segment. Business justification: Risk appetite limits are cascaded to customer segments (e.g., retail mortgage segment concentration limit, SME unsecured lending limit). Risk committees set segment-level limits as part of the RAF (Ri

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: risk_limit has a stress_test_limit_flag (BOOLEAN) indicating that certain limits are specifically defined for stress testing contexts. Adding stress_scenario_id allows stress-specific limits to be sco

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: The approved maximum exposure threshold expressed as an absolute monetary or notional amount in the limit currency. Represents the binding constraint against which utilization is measured. For VaR limits this is the maximum permissible loss; for credit limits this is the maximum Exposure at Default (EAD).
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: Name or title of the governance body or individual who approved this risk limit (e.g., 'ALCO', 'Board Risk Committee', 'CRO', 'Head of Market Risk'). Required for governance audit trail and escalation chain documentation.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; SOX Section 302/404; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk limit was formally approved by the designated approval authority. Establishes the governance record for regulatory examination and internal audit purposes.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: breach_action_rule
attributes.description: Prescribed remediation action protocol to be executed upon a breach event (e.g., 'Immediate escalation to CRO and ALCO; position reduction within 24 hours; SAR filing if AML threshold exceeded'). Codifies the breach governance framework for operational consistency.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing; FinCEN SAR Requirements

attributes.name: breach_count
attributes.description: Cumulative number of breach events recorded against this limit since its effective date. Used for trend analysis, KRI monitoring, and regulatory reporting on limit governance effectiveness.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk limit record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory record-keeping requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the limit amount is denominated (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP'). Required for multi-currency limit consolidation and FX-adjusted utilization calculations.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: current_utilization_amount
attributes.description: The most recently calculated utilization of the limit expressed in the limit currency. Represents the current exposure measured on the utilization_basis (e.g., current VaR, current EAD, current RWA). Updated by the risk management platform on the monitoring frequency cycle.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; SAS Risk Management

attributes.name: desk_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the trading desk or business unit responsible for the positions subject to this limit. Aligns with desk hierarchy in Murex/Calypso trading and order management systems. Required for FRTB desk-level capital attribution.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the risk limit becomes binding and active for utilization monitoring. Aligns with the approval date or the start of the applicable risk period (e.g., fiscal quarter, regulatory reporting period).
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_level_1
attributes.description: Name or role title of the first-level escalation contact notified upon a limit warning or breach event (e.g., 'Head of Market Risk', 'Senior Credit Officer'). Defines the escalation chain for breach governance.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_level_2
attributes.description: Name or role title of the second-level escalation contact notified if the breach is not remediated within the prescribed timeframe (e.g., 'Chief Risk Officer', 'Board Risk Committee Chair'). Supports multi-tier breach governance.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the risk limit ceases to be binding. Null for open-ended standing limits. Limits approaching expiry trigger renewal workflows in the governance framework. Supports regulatory capital constraint management under Basel III/FRTB.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: geography_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country or region code identifying the geographic scope of the limit (e.g., 'USA', 'GBR', 'DEU'). Used for country risk concentration limits and cross-border exposure management.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Country Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: hard_stop_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the limit enforces a hard stop (True) that prevents new transactions from being booked once the limit is reached, or a soft limit (False) that triggers alerts and escalation but does not block transactions. Critical for real-time limit monitoring integration with trading and order management systems.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS FRTB

attributes.name: last_breach_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent breach event recorded against this limit. Null if no breach has occurred. Used for recency analysis in KRI dashboards and regulatory examination responses.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

attributes.name: limit_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the risk limit (e.g., 'CRED-CORP-001', 'MKT-VAR-DESK-FX-002'). Used in regulatory submissions, audit trails, and cross-system references. Aligns with the limit reference code maintained in SAS Risk Management / Moody's RiskAuthority.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; OCC Risk Management Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: limit_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the business rationale, scope, and any special conditions or exclusions applicable to this risk limit. Provides context for governance reviews, regulatory examinations, and audit inquiries.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: limit_name
attributes.description: Descriptive business name of the risk limit (e.g., 'FX Trading Desk Daily VaR Limit', 'Corporate Credit Concentration Limit — Technology Sector'). Used in dashboards, governance reports, and ALCO presentations.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Handbook — Risk Management

attributes.name: limit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the risk limit record. 'active' indicates the limit is in force and being monitored; 'suspended' indicates temporary hold pending review; 'breached' indicates the limit is currently in excess; 'pending_approval' indicates awaiting governance sign-off.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the risk limit by risk category. Drives applicable measurement methodology and regulatory capital treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: credit|market|liquidity|concentration|operational|counterparty|country|sector|settlement|intraday — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the Line of Business (LOB) responsible for managing and consuming this risk limit (e.g., 'IB-EQUITIES', 'RETAIL-LENDING', 'CORP-CREDIT', 'TREASURY'). Used for LOB-level risk appetite reporting and CCAR/DFAST segmentation.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Guidance; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Basel III

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which utilization is recalculated and compared against the limit threshold (e.g., 'real_time' for trading desk VaR limits, 'daily' for credit concentration limits, 'monthly' for LCR/NSFR limits). Drives the monitoring schedule in the risk management platform.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: regulatory_capital_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this limit is directly tied to a regulatory capital constraint (True) under Basel III/FRTB (e.g., RWA limit, CET1 buffer limit, LCR minimum). Flags limits that require regulatory reporting upon breach.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency at which the risk limit is formally reviewed and reaffirmed by the approving authority. Drives governance calendar and ALCO agenda scheduling.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

attributes.name: scope_entity_type
attributes.description: The type of business entity to which this limit applies. Determines the dimension of risk aggregation (e.g., 'counterparty' for single-name credit limits, 'desk' for trading desk VaR limits, 'lob' for Line of Business concentration limits, 'geography' for country risk limits). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: counterparty|portfolio|desk|lob|geography|sector|instrument|legal_entity — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this limit record originates (e.g., 'SAS-RISK', 'MOODYS-RA', 'MUREX', 'AXIOMSL'). Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; SOX Section 302/404; BCBS Basel III

attributes.name: stress_test_limit_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this limit is a stress-scenario limit (True) applied under CCAR/DFAST stress testing frameworks, as opposed to a business-as-usual (BAU) limit. Stress limits typically have higher thresholds and different breach protocols.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing; Dodd-Frank Act Section 165

attributes.name: subtype
attributes.description: Further granular classification within the limit type (e.g., 'VaR', 'CVA', 'PV01', 'DV01', 'ECL', 'RWA', 'LCR', 'NSFR', 'Single-Name Concentration', 'Sector Concentration'). Enables drill-down analytics and precise regulatory mapping.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB; BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk limit record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks limit amendments, utilization updates, and status changes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

attributes.name: utilization_as_of_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the current utilization amount was calculated or sourced from the risk management platform. Critical for intraday limit monitoring and audit trail integrity. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: utilization_basis
attributes.description: The measurement methodology used to calculate current utilization against the limit. Determines which risk metric is compared to the limit amount (e.g., 'var' for Value at Risk limits, 'ead' for Exposure at Default credit limits, 'rwa' for Risk-Weighted Asset limits, 'lcr_outflow' for liquidity limits). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: notional|mtm|ead|var|rwa|ecl|nii_impact|lcr_outflow|cva|pv01|dv01 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: utilization_pct
attributes.description: Current utilization expressed as a percentage of the approved limit amount (current_utilization_amount / limit_amount × 100). Enables threshold-based alerting and trend analysis. Values above 100 indicate a breach condition.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: var_confidence_level
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level used in the VaR calculation for market risk limits (e.g., 99.00 for 99th percentile, 97.50 for 97.5th percentile as required under FRTB Expected Shortfall). Applicable only for market risk limit types with VaR/ES utilization basis.
attributes.references: BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: var_holding_period_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: Value at Risk (VaR) Holding Period Days
attributes.description: The holding period in calendar days used in the VaR calculation for market risk limits (e.g., 1 for daily VaR, 10 for 10-day regulatory VaR under Basel III). Applicable only for market risk limit types.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; BCBS FRTB; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: warning_threshold_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the limit amount at which an early-warning alert is triggered (e.g., 80.00 for 80%). Enables proactive escalation before a formal breach occurs. Expressed as a percentage (0–100). Configured per limit in SAS Risk Management / Moody's RiskAuthority.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Risk Management Guidance; BCBS Principles for Sound Stress Testing

products.name: credit_exposure
products.description: Transactional record of credit exposure measurement, risk-weighted asset (RWA) calculation, and counterparty credit valuation adjustment (CVA) for obligors, counterparties, and portfolios. For exposure measurement: captures current exposure, potential future exposure (PFE), expected exposure (EE), EAD, netting set identifiers, collateral offsets, and exposure by regulatory approach (SA and IRB). For RWA: captures credit, market, and operational RWA by portfolio, asset class, and regulatory framework (Basel III/CRR2), with capital ratios (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital) and Pillar 3 disclosure metadata. For CVA: captures CVA, DVA, FVA for OTC derivative counterparty credit risk including counterparty PD, LGD, expected exposure profile, netting set, CSA terms, hedging instruments, and regulatory CVA capital charge under SA-CVA/BA-CVA. Includes concentration risk metrics: single-name, sector, geographic, and product concentration exposures, HHI, and regulatory large exposure reporting under CRR Article 395. Primary input to CCAR/DFAST stress testing, ECL provisioning, and concentration limit monitoring. Sourced from Murex/Calypso and SAS Risk Management.

attributes.name: collateral_value
attributes.description: Current market value of eligible financial collateral posted against this exposure after applicable haircuts under the Financial Collateral Comprehensive Method (FCCM). Reduces EAD and RWA.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE22 — Credit Risk Mitigation; CRR2 Articles 197-217; BCBS Haircut Framework

attributes.name: concentration_hhi
attributes.description: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index score measuring the degree of concentration of this exposure within its sector, geography, or single-name bucket. Used for concentration risk monitoring and regulatory large exposure limit compliance.

attributes.name: counterparty_type
attributes.description: Classification of the counterparty for regulatory capital and large exposure reporting purposes. Determines applicable risk weight under SA and eligibility for IRB treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corporate|financial_institution|sovereign|central_bank|retail|sme|fund — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS CRE20; CRR2 Article 112; FINRA Counterparty Classification

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this credit exposure record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under SOX and Basel Pillar 3.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS BCBS239 — Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting

attributes.name: current_exposure
attributes.description: Current mark-to-market (MTM) replacement cost of the exposure as of the measurement date, before netting and collateral. For derivatives, represents the positive MTM value. For loans, represents the outstanding principal balance.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE53 — SA-CCR Current Exposure; ISDA Credit Support Annex; Murex MTM Module

attributes.name: cva
attributes.description: Market value of counterparty credit risk embedded in OTC derivative positions, representing the expected loss due to counterparty default. Calculated under SA-CVA or BA-CVA regulatory framework. Impacts P&L and regulatory capital.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE51 — CVA Risk Framework; CRR2 Article 381; IFRS 13 Fair Value; ISDA CVA Standard

attributes.name: cva_approach
attributes.description: Regulatory methodology used to calculate the CVA capital charge: Standardised Approach for CVA (SA-CVA), Basic Approach for CVA (BA-CVA), or exempted (for transactions with non-financial counterparties below threshold).
attributes.references: BCBS CRE51 — CVA Framework; CRR2 Articles 382-386

attributes.name: cva_capital_charge
attributes.description: Regulatory capital requirement for CVA risk calculated under SA-CVA or BA-CVA methodology as prescribed by BCBS CRE51. Represents the RWA equivalent for counterparty credit valuation adjustment risk.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE51 — SA-CVA/BA-CVA Capital Charge; CRR2 Article 383; Basel III Final Rule

attributes.name: dva
attributes.description: Adjustment to derivative fair value reflecting the bank's own credit risk, representing the benefit to the bank from its own potential default. Reported under IFRS 13 but excluded from regulatory CVA capital charge.
attributes.references: IFRS 13 — Fair Value Measurement; BCBS CRE51; ISDA DVA Standard

attributes.name: ead
attributes.description: Estimated total exposure amount outstanding at the time of default, expressed in the reporting currency. Incorporates credit conversion factors (CCF) for off-balance-sheet items and SA-CCR replacement cost for derivatives. Core input to RWA and ECL calculation.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE36.88 — EAD Estimation; CRR2 Article 166; SA-CCR CRE52

attributes.name: effective_maturity_years
attributes.description: Effective maturity parameter (M) in years as defined under the IRB Advanced approach, capped at 5 years and floored at 1 year. Adjusts the IRB capital formula for longer-dated exposures via the maturity adjustment factor.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE36.93 — Effective Maturity; CRR2 Article 162

attributes.name: expected_exposure
attributes.description: Average exposure across all simulation paths at a future time horizon, used as the basis for CVA calculation and expected credit loss (ECL) provisioning under IFRS 9.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE53 — Expected Exposure Profile; IFRS 9 ECL; SA-CVA CRE51

attributes.name: exposure_class
attributes.description: Regulatory asset class of the exposure under Basel III/CRR2 framework, determining the applicable risk weight and capital treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corporate|sovereign|institution|retail|equity|securitisation|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS CRE20 — Standardised Approach; CRR2 Article 112; Basel III Final Rule

attributes.name: exposure_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business reference number for this credit exposure record, as assigned by the risk management platform (SAS Risk Management / Moodys RiskAuthority) or trading system (Murex/Calypso). Used for reconciliation and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: SAS Risk Management — Exposure Reference; Murex Credit Risk Module

attributes.name: exposure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the credit exposure. Drives provisioning, regulatory classification, and workout processes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|closed|defaulted|restructured|watch_list|written_off — promote to reference product if additional states required]
attributes.references: BCBS CRE — Credit Risk Classification; IFRS 9 Stage Classification; OCC Loan Classification Guidelines

attributes.name: fva
attributes.description: Adjustment to derivative fair value reflecting the cost or benefit of funding uncollateralised derivative positions. Captures the funding spread between the bank's borrowing cost and the risk-free rate.
attributes.references: IFRS 13 — Fair Value Measurement; ISDA FVA Framework; Basel III Funding Cost

attributes.name: fx_rate
attributes.description: Exchange rate applied to translate the exposure from its original currency to the reporting currency as of the measurement date. Sourced from the bank's official FX rate feed.
attributes.references: BCBS FX Risk; CRR2 Article 352; ECB Reference Rates

attributes.name: large_exposure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exposure meets or exceeds the large exposure threshold (10% of eligible capital) requiring regulatory reporting under CRR2 Article 395. Triggers enhanced monitoring and reporting obligations.
attributes.references: CRR2 Article 395 — Large Exposures Limit; EBA GL/2021/07; BCBS Large Exposures Standard

attributes.name: lgd
attributes.description: Estimated fraction of the Exposure at Default (EAD) that would be lost in the event of default, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.45 = 45%). Reflects collateral, seniority, and recovery assumptions under IRB Advanced approach.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE36.83 — LGD Estimation; IFRS 9 ECL; CECL ASC 326; OCC LGD Guidance

attributes.name: maturity_date
attributes.description: Contractual maturity date of the underlying credit facility or instrument. Used to calculate effective maturity (M) for IRB capital calculation and to determine the exposure's remaining tenor for PFE and CVA profiles.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE36.93 — Effective Maturity; CRR2 Article 162; Finastra Loan IQ Maturity Date

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.description: The as-of date on which the credit exposure was measured and calculated. Represents the principal business event date for this record. Used for point-in-time regulatory reporting (CCAR, DFAST, Pillar 3).
attributes.references: BCBS CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing Guidelines; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: net_exposure
attributes.description: Credit exposure after applying netting agreements and eligible collateral offsets (EAD minus collateral value). Represents the bank's actual economic risk position used for limit monitoring and large exposure reporting.
attributes.references: CRR2 Article 395 — Large Exposures; BCBS CRE22 — Netting and Collateral; ISDA Netting Opinion

attributes.name: pd
attributes.description: Estimated probability that the obligor will default within a one-year horizon, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.00250 = 0.25%). Core IRB parameter used in RWA and ECL calculation under IFRS 9 and CECL.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE36.46 — PD Estimation; IFRS 9 — Expected Credit Loss; CECL ASC 326

attributes.name: pillar3_disclosure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exposure record is included in the bank's Pillar 3 public disclosure reporting under Basel III. Drives the regulatory reporting extract for AxiomSL/Wolters Kluwer OneSumX.
attributes.references: BCBS Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements (January 2015, updated 2018); CRR2 Article 431

attributes.name: potential_future_exposure
attributes.description: Estimated maximum exposure at a specified confidence level (typically 95%) over the remaining life of the transaction, capturing future market movements. Used in counterparty credit limit monitoring and CVA calculation.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE53 — SA-CCR PFE Add-on; ISDA SIMM; Murex/Calypso PFE Engine

attributes.name: regulatory_approach
attributes.description: Regulatory methodology applied to calculate risk-weighted assets (RWA) for this exposure: Standardised Approach (SA), Foundation Internal Ratings-Based (F-IRB), Advanced IRB (A-IRB), Standardised Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR), or Internal Model Method (IMM).
attributes.references: BCBS CRE — IRB Approach; CRR2 Articles 143-191; Basel III Final Rule

attributes.name: reporting_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the bank's reporting currency into which all exposure amounts are translated for regulatory capital and Pillar 3 reporting (typically USD or EUR).
attributes.references: ISO 4217; BCBS Pillar 3 Disclosure Requirements; CRR2 Article 430

attributes.name: risk_weight
attributes.description: Risk weight percentage applied to the exposure to derive credit RWA, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 1.00 = 100%). Determined by exposure class, counterparty rating, and regulatory approach (SA or IRB).
attributes.references: BCBS CRE20 — SA Risk Weights; CRR2 Articles 114-134; Basel III Final Rule

attributes.name: rwa_credit
attributes.description: Risk-weighted asset amount for credit risk calculated for this exposure under the applicable regulatory approach (SA or IRB). Primary input to CET1 capital ratio calculation and Pillar 3 disclosure.
attributes.references: BCBS CRE — RWA Calculation; CRR2 Article 92; Basel III Final Rule; CCAR/DFAST Capital Planning

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this credit exposure record was sourced (e.g., Murex/Calypso for derivatives, Finastra Loan IQ for loans, SAS Risk Management for aggregated risk). Supports data lineage and BCBS 239 compliance.
attributes.references: BCBS 239 — Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Principles; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this credit exposure record was last modified or recalculated. Tracks recalibration events, model updates, and data corrections.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS239 — Risk Data Aggregation

products.name: market_risk_position
products.description: Daily mark-to-market risk position record for trading book and banking book instruments. For trading book: captures MTM value, VaR (historical simulation, Monte Carlo, parametric), stressed VaR, IRC, sensitivity measures (DV01, CS01, delta, gamma, vega), P&L attribution, and FRTB IMA/SA capital charges. For banking book (IRRBB): captures repricing gap analysis, NII sensitivity, EVE sensitivity, basis risk, optionality risk, yield curve shock scenarios (parallel shift, twist, steepener, flattener), NII at risk, EVE at risk, and BCBS IRRBB standard compliance metrics. Sourced from Murex/Calypso trading system and SAS Risk Management. Supports ALCO reporting, treasury ALM coordination, FRTB regulatory submissions, and IRRBB supervisory outlier test compliance.

attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the position as either trading book (subject to market risk capital under FRTB) or banking book (subject to IRRBB framework). Determines applicable capital treatment and risk measurement methodology.
