attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_exam. Business justification: Regulatory-reportable op risk events (regulatory_reportable_indicator=Y) are directly cited in regulatory examinations. Examiners request op risk event logs during CAMELS/SREP reviews. The regulatory_

attributes.name: settlement_instruction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trade.settlement_instruction. Business justification: Settlement failures are a major operational risk category under CSDR penalty regime. Linking operational_risk_event to the failed settlement_instruction enables CSDR penalty loss tracking, Basel SMA o

attributes.name: status_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to payment.status_event. Business justification: Payment status exceptions, SLA breaches, and system-generated error events are operational risk events under Basel 'Business Disruption and System Failures' category. This link enables operational ris

attributes.name: accounting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operational risk loss was recognized in the general ledger and financial statements. Used for IFRS 9 / CECL provisioning alignment and financial reporting reconciliation.
attributes.references: IFRS 9 — Financial Instruments; FASB ASC 450 Contingencies; BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the operational risk event record was formally reviewed and approved by the designated risk manager or senior officer. Supports audit trail and governance requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; OCC Supervisory Guidance; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices

attributes.name: basel_event_type_category
attributes.description: Basel III Level 1 operational risk event type category classification. Values: 'internal_fraud' (Internal Fraud), 'external_fraud' (External Fraud), 'epws' (Employment Practices and Workplace Safety), 'cpbp' (Clients Products and Business Practices), 'edpm' (Execution Delivery and Process Management), 'bdsf' (Business Disruption and System Failures), 'eflf' (Damage to Physical Assets). Mandatory for SMA capital charge calculation and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: internal_fraud|external_fraud|epws|cpbp|edpm|bdsf|eflf — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Annex 9 Operational Risk Event Type Classification; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: basel_event_type_level2
attributes.description: Basel III Level 2 sub-category providing granular classification within the Level 1 event type (e.g., 'Unauthorized Activity' under Internal Fraud, 'Theft and Fraud' under External Fraud, 'Suitability Disclosure and Fiduciary' under CPBP). Supports detailed root cause analysis and trend reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product aligned with BCBS Annex 9 taxonomy]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Annex 9 Level 2 Event Type Sub-Categories

attributes.name: causal_factor_code
attributes.description: Standardized code from the enterprise causal factor taxonomy identifying the specific contributing factor(s) to the operational risk event (e.g., inadequate segregation of duties, system configuration error, third-party vendor failure, inadequate staff training). Used for trend analysis and KRI calibration.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; GRC Platform — Moodys RiskAuthority Causal Factor Taxonomy

attributes.name: ccar_dfast_applicable_indicator
attributes.business_glossary_term: Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review / Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing (CCAR/DFAST) Applicable Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this operational risk event is included in the operational risk loss scenario library used for CCAR and DFAST stress testing submissions to the Federal Reserve. Supports capital adequacy assessment under stressed conditions.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Framework; Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing (DFAST) Requirements; Federal Reserve SR 15-18

attributes.name: control_failure_type
attributes.description: Classification of the internal control failure that contributed to the operational risk event. 'design_failure' indicates the control was inadequately designed; 'operating_failure' indicates the control existed but did not operate effectively; 'no_control' indicates absence of a required control; 'override' indicates management override of controls; 'circumvention' indicates deliberate bypass of controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control Framework; OCC Supervisory Guidance; BCBS Operational Risk

attributes.name: corrective_action_due_date
attributes.description: Target completion date for the corrective action plan associated with this operational risk event. Used for management escalation tracking and regulatory examination readiness.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance; SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control Framework

attributes.name: corrective_action_status
attributes.description: Status of the corrective action plan (CAP) initiated in response to the operational risk event to remediate the identified control failure. 'not_required' for near-miss events with no control gap; 'planned' for CAP defined but not started; 'in_progress' for active remediation; 'completed' for fully remediated; 'overdue' for past target completion date.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control Framework

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the operational risk event record was first captured and persisted in the GRC platform or internal loss database. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards

attributes.name: discovery_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operational risk event was first identified or discovered by the bank, which may differ significantly from the event date for latent losses. Used to measure detection lag and assess control effectiveness.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; Moodys RiskAuthority — Loss Event Capture

attributes.name: event_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operational risk loss event actually occurred or commenced. This is the principal real-world event date used for SMA capital charge period allocation and regulatory reporting. Distinct from discovery date and accounting date.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA); BCBS 196 Operational Risk Data Collection Exercise

attributes.name: event_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the operational risk event, including what happened, how it was identified, and the immediate impact. Supports root cause analysis, regulatory examination responses, and internal audit reviews.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; PRA SS1/23; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: event_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the operational risk event by the GRC platform or internal loss database (e.g., ORE-2024-00123). Used for cross-system reconciliation and regulatory reporting submissions to OCC/Fed/PRA.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; OCC Bulletin 2019-37; PRA SS1/23

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the operational risk event record. 'open' indicates active loss event under investigation; 'under_review' indicates root cause analysis in progress; 'closed' indicates fully resolved and signed off; 'near_miss' indicates no financial loss but control failure identified; 'pending_recovery' indicates awaiting insurance or third-party recovery.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; SAS Risk Management — Loss Event Workflow

attributes.name: event_title
attributes.description: Short, descriptive title summarizing the nature of the operational risk event (e.g., 'Unauthorized Wire Transfer — Treasury Operations', 'System Outage — Payment Processing Hub'). Used for management reporting and GRC dashboard display.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; GRC Platform — Moodys RiskAuthority

attributes.name: external_loss_database_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this internal loss event to a corresponding record in an external operational risk loss data consortium (e.g., ORX — Operational Riskdata eXchange Association). Supports benchmarking of internal loss experience against industry peers.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices — Use of External Data; ORX Loss Data Standards

attributes.name: gross_loss_amount
attributes.description: Total gross financial loss incurred from the operational risk event before any recoveries, expressed in the reporting currency. This is the primary input to the SMA capital charge calculation and must meet the BCBS minimum loss threshold for regulatory reporting (typically USD 20,000 for internal data collection).
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA Capital Charge; BCBS 196 Operational Risk Data Collection; OCC Reporting

attributes.name: insurance_recovery_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the total recovery amount attributable specifically to insurance policy payouts (e.g., fidelity bond, professional indemnity, cyber insurance). Tracked separately per BCBS guidance on insurance recognition in operational risk capital.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Insurance Recognition in Operational Risk; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: legal_action_status
attributes.description: Status of any legal proceedings or litigation associated with the operational risk event. 'none' indicates no legal action; 'threatened' indicates potential litigation notified; 'filed' indicates lawsuit filed; 'settled' indicates out-of-court settlement reached; 'judgment' indicates court judgment rendered; 'dismissed' indicates case dismissed.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 450 Contingencies; IFRS IAS 37 Provisions; OCC Supervisory Guidance; SOX

attributes.name: legal_provision_amount
attributes.description: Financial provision or reserve established in the general ledger for potential legal liability arising from the operational risk event. Recognized per IFRS IAS 37 or FASB ASC 450 when outflow is probable and estimable.
attributes.references: IFRS IAS 37 Provisions Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets; FASB ASC 450; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: loss_recovery_date
attributes.description: Date on which the recovery amount was received or recognized, whether from insurance, legal settlement, or third-party reimbursement. Used for cash flow timing analysis and SMA recovery component allocation.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA Recovery Component; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices

attributes.name: loss_threshold_met_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the gross loss amount meets or exceeds the minimum loss data threshold (typically USD 20,000 per BCBS guidance) required for inclusion in the SMA Loss Component calculation and external loss data consortium submissions.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA; BCBS 196 Operational Risk Data Collection Exercise

attributes.name: near_miss_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this record represents a near-miss incident (potential loss that was averted) rather than an actual realized loss event. Near-miss events have zero gross loss but are captured for control environment assessment and KRI monitoring.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk

attributes.name: net_loss_amount
attributes.description: Net financial loss after deducting all recoveries from the gross loss amount (gross_loss_amount minus recovery_amount). This is the final economic impact figure used for P&L attribution, RAROC calculation, and management reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA; IFRS 9; FASB ASC 450

attributes.name: recovery_amount
attributes.description: Total amount recovered from all sources (insurance, legal settlements, third-party reimbursements, collateral liquidation) following the operational risk loss event. Subtracted from gross loss to derive net loss.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this operational risk event meets the threshold or criteria requiring mandatory regulatory reporting to OCC, Federal Reserve, PRA, or other supervisory authorities (e.g., significant operational events, cyber incidents, large losses).
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; PRA SS1/23; BCBS Operational Risk

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level root cause classification of the operational risk event following root cause analysis (RCA). Standard taxonomy: 'people' (human error, misconduct, inadequate training), 'process' (process failure, inadequate controls, procedural breach), 'system' (IT system failure, data quality, cybersecurity), 'external_event' (natural disaster, third-party failure, fraud by external party).
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; ISO 31000 Risk Management; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the root cause analysis findings, identifying the specific underlying cause(s) of the operational risk event. Supports corrective action planning, control remediation, and regulatory examination responses.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; PRA SS1/23; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: sma_loss_component
attributes.description: Classification of how this event contributes to the SMA capital charge calculation under Basel III. 'loss_component' indicates the event feeds the Loss Component (LC) of the SMA formula; 'recovery_component' indicates a recovery adjustment; 'timing_adjustment' indicates a multi-year loss requiring temporal allocation per BCBS guidance.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) for Operational Risk; BCBS d355

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the originating operational system from which this loss event record was sourced (e.g., MOODYS_RISK_AUTHORITY, SAS_RISK_MGMT, GRC_PLATFORM, MANUAL_ENTRY). Used for data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards; SOX Section 404 — Data Lineage

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the operational risk event record, including updates to loss amounts, recovery amounts, root cause classification, or status changes. Supports audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk

products.name: kri_measurement
products.description: Key Risk Indicator (KRI) master registry and periodic measurement record. Captures KRI definitions (name, risk category, calculation methodology, measurement frequency, data source, green/amber/red thresholds, owner, escalation path) and periodic readings (measurement date, actual value, threshold breach status, trend direction, owning business unit, escalation status). Links to risk appetite framework for threshold derivation. Provides the authoritative KRI taxonomy and monitoring data for enterprise risk dashboards, GRC reporting, and board risk committee oversight.

attributes.name: kri_measurement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each KRI measurement record in the enterprise risk monitoring registry. Primary key for the kri_measurement data product.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Principles for Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239)

attributes.name: accounting_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.accounting_period. Business justification: Board risk reporting and regulatory KRI submissions (SREP, ICAAP) align KRI measurements to financial accounting periods for period-over-period trend analysis. measurement_period_start/end are plain d

attributes.name: appetite_id

attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: assessment_id

attributes.name: branch_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.branch. Business justification: Branch-level KRI scorecards are a standard banking practice — regulators and internal audit track KRIs (fraud rate, complaint volume, cash discrepancy) at individual branch level. Existing channel_id

attributes.name: capital_ratio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.capital_ratio. Business justification: Capital ratio KRIs (CET1 ratio, leverage ratio, total capital ratio) are measured directly against capital_ratio records. Linking kri_measurement to capital_ratio enables direct traceability from KRI

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Key Risk Indicators are measured per channel (ATM downtime %, digital fraud rate, branch error rate). Channel-level KRI monitoring is standard in banking risk management for operational risk oversight

attributes.name: fund_performance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.fund_performance. Business justification: Investment risk KRIs (tracking error breach, maximum drawdown, Sharpe ratio threshold) are measured directly from fund performance records. Risk teams configure KRIs that trigger when fund_performance

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: ICAAP and SREP regulatory submissions require KRI measurements to be attributed to specific legal entities. The plain column legal_entity on kri_measurement is a denormalized string; replacing with a

attributes.name: liquidity_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.liquidity_position. Business justification: KRIs monitor specific liquidity position metrics for early warning indicators in risk appetite framework. Liquidity KRIs track intraday positions, tenor gaps, and scenario-based positions for breach d

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: KRIs are defined to measure adherence to specific regulatory obligations (e.g., LCR KRI tied to Basel III liquidity obligation, capital ratio KRI tied to CRR capital obligation). Compliance teams use

attributes.name: risk_limit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_limit. Business justification: KRI measurements track against defined thresholds and limits. The kri_measurement table has green/amber/red thresholds and breach_status — these are operationally linked to risk_limit definitions for

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: kri_measurement has stress_scenario_flag (BOOLEAN) and stress_scenario_name (STRING) as denormalized references to a stress scenario. Adding stress_scenario_id normalizes this relationship, allowing K

attributes.name: actual_value
attributes.description: The observed or calculated numeric value of the KRI for the measurement period. Represents the raw measurement result before threshold comparison (e.g., NPL ratio of 0.0325, LCR of 1.42, VaR of 15000000). Unit of measure is defined in the unit_of_measure field.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: amber_threshold
attributes.description: The boundary defining the warning (amber) zone for the KRI. Values breaching this threshold trigger heightened monitoring and management attention but do not yet require board-level escalation. Derived from the risk appetite framework.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Workflow status of the KRI measurement record through the review and approval process. 'draft' indicates initial capture, 'submitted' indicates pending review, 'approved' indicates sign-off by risk governance, 'rejected' indicates the measurement requires correction and resubmission.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302/404

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the KRI measurement record was formally approved by the risk governance officer. Provides the audit timestamp for SOX and regulatory compliance purposes.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302/404; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the risk governance officer who approved this KRI measurement record. Required for SOX and regulatory audit trail. Classified confidential as it identifies internal personnel.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302/404; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: breach_status
attributes.description: The RAG (Red-Amber-Green) status of the KRI measurement relative to defined thresholds. 'green' indicates within appetite, 'amber' indicates warning zone, 'red' indicates limit breach. Drives escalation workflows and board risk committee reporting.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR Guidance

attributes.name: calculation_methodology
attributes.description: Description of the methodology or formula used to calculate the KRI value (e.g., 'HQLA / Net Cash Outflows over 30 days', 'NPL balance / Total Gross Loans', '99th percentile 10-day VaR using historical simulation'). Supports model governance and audit requirements.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

attributes.name: commentary
attributes.description: Free-text narrative commentary provided by the KRI owner explaining the measurement result, contextualising any threshold breaches, or noting exceptional circumstances affecting the value (e.g., market dislocation, one-off events, methodology changes).
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this KRI measurement record was first created in the system. Provides the audit creation timestamp for data lineage, BCBS 239 compliance, and silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Categorical data quality assessment for this KRI measurement record. 'passed' indicates data meets quality standards, 'warning' indicates minor data issues that do not invalidate the measurement, 'failed' indicates the measurement should not be used, 'under_review' indicates quality assessment is pending.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: A numeric score (0.00 to 100.00) representing the assessed quality of the underlying data used to compute this KRI measurement. Supports BCBS 239 data quality attestation requirements and flags measurements with low data confidence for review.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239 Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which the KRI measurement data was sourced (e.g., 'SAS Risk Management', 'Moodys RiskAuthority', 'Murex', 'Core Banking T24', 'AxiomSL'). Critical for data lineage and BCBS 239 data quality attestation.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: escalation_authority
attributes.description: The governance body or individual to whom the KRI breach has been escalated (e.g., 'ALCO', 'Board Risk Committee', 'CRO', 'Risk Management Committee'). Defines the escalation path for each breach severity level.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Corporate Governance Principles for Banks

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the KRI breach was formally escalated to the designated escalation authority. Null if no escalation was required. Used to measure escalation timeliness against SLA targets.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the escalation workflow triggered by a KRI breach. 'not_required' for green-status KRIs, 'pending' when escalation has been initiated but not yet actioned, 'in_progress' when remediation is underway, 'resolved' when breach is remediated, 'overdue' when SLA has been breached.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Governance Risk and Compliance (GRC) Framework

attributes.name: green_threshold
attributes.description: The upper or lower boundary defining the acceptable (green) zone for the KRI. Values within this threshold indicate normal operating conditions and no escalation is required. Derived from the risk appetite framework.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: is_board_reported
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI is included in board risk committee reporting packs (True) or is management-level only (False). Board-reported KRIs require higher data quality standards and formal sign-off per governance policy.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Corporate Governance Principles for Banks; Financial Stability Board (FSB)

attributes.name: is_regulatory_kri
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI is mandated by a regulatory body (True) or is an internally-defined management KRI (False). Regulatory KRIs (e.g., LCR, CET1, NSFR) require formal regulatory reporting and have prescribed minimum thresholds.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)

attributes.name: kri_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the KRI definition in the enterprise KRI taxonomy. Follows the format KRI-<CATEGORY>-<SEQUENCE> (e.g., KRI-CREDIT-0001). Links the measurement to the KRI master registry entry.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

attributes.name: kri_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the KRI being measured (e.g., 'Non-Performing Loan Ratio', 'Liquidity Coverage Ratio', 'Value at Risk Utilisation'). Sourced from the KRI master registry.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: kri_owner_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual accountable for the KRI measurement, remediation, and escalation. Typically a senior risk officer or business unit head. Classified confidential as it identifies internal accountability assignments.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Governance Guidelines

attributes.name: kri_owner_role
attributes.description: The job title or role designation of the KRI owner (e.g., 'Chief Risk Officer', 'Head of Credit Risk', 'Treasury Risk Manager'). Supports role-based escalation routing and governance reporting.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Corporate Governance Principles for Banks

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.description: The business date on which the KRI value was observed or calculated. Represents the as-of date for the measurement, distinct from the record creation timestamp. Critical for time-series trend analysis and regulatory reporting periods.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: measurement_frequency
attributes.description: The prescribed frequency at which this KRI is measured and reported. Determines the cadence of data collection and dashboard refresh cycles (e.g., LCR is measured daily, NSFR monthly, ICAAP KRIs quarterly).
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III LCR/NSFR Standards; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR Annual Cycle

attributes.name: measurement_period_end
attributes.description: The end date of the measurement period over which the KRI value was calculated. For point-in-time KRIs this equals measurement_date; for flow-based KRIs this defines the close of the accumulation window.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 825

attributes.name: measurement_period_start
attributes.description: The start date of the measurement period over which the KRI value was calculated. For point-in-time KRIs this equals measurement_date; for flow-based KRIs (e.g., monthly loss events) this defines the beginning of the accumulation window.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 825

attributes.name: owning_business_unit
attributes.description: The line of business (LOB) or organisational unit responsible for managing and remediating this KRI (e.g., 'Commercial Lending', 'Treasury', 'Retail Banking', 'Trading'). Used for accountability assignment in GRC reporting and board risk committee packs.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Assessment System

attributes.name: prior_period_value
attributes.description: The KRI actual value from the immediately preceding measurement period. Stored on the record to support period-over-period variance analysis and trend computation without requiring a self-join. Expressed in the same unit_of_measure as actual_value.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Reporting

attributes.name: red_threshold
attributes.description: The boundary defining the breach (red) zone for the KRI. Values exceeding this threshold indicate a material risk limit breach requiring immediate escalation to senior management or the board risk committee.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Free-text description of the management action plan or remediation steps being taken to address a KRI breach or amber warning. Captured for audit trail and board risk committee reporting purposes.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Assessment System

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: The target date by which the remediation action for a KRI breach must be completed. Used to track SLA compliance and flag overdue escalations in GRC dashboards.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: High-level risk taxonomy category to which this KRI belongs. Aligns with the enterprise risk taxonomy and Basel III risk classification framework. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: credit|market|liquidity|operational|compliance|reputational|strategic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III Framework; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: risk_sub_category
attributes.description: Granular risk sub-classification within the risk category (e.g., 'counterparty credit risk', 'interest rate risk in the banking book', 'settlement risk', 'conduct risk'). Supports drill-down analysis in GRC reporting.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III Framework; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Assessment System

attributes.name: stress_scenario_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this measurement record represents a stress scenario value (True) rather than a base-case actual measurement (False). Stress scenario KRI readings are used in CCAR, DFAST, and ICAAP submissions.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing Requirements; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: threshold_direction

products.name: scenario_appetite_result
products.description: This association product represents the formal stress test result event between a stress_scenario and a risk appetite statement. It captures the outcome of evaluating a specific stress scenario against a specific appetite metric — including the stressed metric value, breach status, and delta to threshold. Each record is a governance-grade result produced during CCAR, DFAST, ICAAP, or internal stress cycles, reviewed by ALCO and the Board. Attributes exist only in the context of this scenario-appetite intersection and cannot reside on either parent entity.. Existence Justification: In enterprise risk management, stress testing scenarios are formally evaluated against each risk appetite statement as part of CCAR/DFAST/ICAAP governance processes. A single stress scenario (e.g., 'Severely Adverse 2024') is tested against MULTIPLE appetite metrics (CET1 floor, LCR, credit loss tolerance, etc.), and each appetite statement is evaluated under MULTIPLE scenarios (baseline, adverse, severely adverse). The business actively manages and reports on these per-scenario, per-appetite results as a formal governance deliverable — this is not an analytical derivation but an operationally produced record reviewed by ALCO and the Board.

attributes.name: breach_indicator

attributes.name: stressed_metric_value
attributes.description: The computed value of the risk appetite metric under the conditions of the linked stress scenario. Belongs to the intersection — the same appetite metric will have a different stressed value under each scenario.

attributes.name: stressed_threshold_delta
attributes.description: The arithmetic difference between the stressed_metric_value and the appetite threshold (limit_value, range_lower_bound, or range_upper_bound as applicable). Negative values indicate headroom; positive values indicate breach magnitude.

attributes.name: rehypothecation_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the collateral taker has the right to rehypothecate (reuse) posted collateral for its own purposes. True = rehypothecation allowed, False = collateral must be segregated.

attributes.name: renewal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the margin agreement is scheduled for renewal or renegotiation. Nullable for agreements without automatic renewal.

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for periodic review of the margin agreement terms, typically annual or biennial.

attributes.name: rounding_convention
attributes.description: Method used to round collateral transfer amounts. NEAREST = round to nearest unit, UP = always round up, DOWN = always round down, NONE = no rounding applied.

attributes.name: rounding_precision
attributes.description: Precision unit for rounding collateral transfer amounts, typically expressed in the settlement currency (e.g., 1000 for rounding to nearest thousand).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system from which this margin agreement record originated (e.g., Murex, Calypso, SAS Risk Management).

attributes.name: substitution_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the collateral provider has the right to substitute posted collateral with other eligible collateral. True = substitution allowed, False = no substitution permitted.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the margin agreement terminates or is scheduled to terminate. Nullable for open-ended agreements.

attributes.name: threshold_amount
attributes.description: Minimum exposure amount below which no collateral is required to be posted. Part of the Credit Support Annex (CSA) terms.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this margin agreement record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: valuation_agent
attributes.description: Entity responsible for determining the value of collateral and exposure. PARTY_A = bank, PARTY_B = counterparty, THIRD_PARTY = independent valuation service, MUTUAL = both parties agree on valuation.

attributes.name: valuation_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which collateral and exposure are revalued for margin call purposes.

attributes.name: variation_margin_settlement_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which variation margin is settled daily to reflect mark-to-market exposure changes.

products.name: collateral_position
products.description: Current inventory snapshot, calculated exposure record, and margin exposure view for collateral held, posted, or received across all arrangements. Captures position date, collateral asset, arrangement reference, position type (held, posted, received, pledged, rehypothecated, exposure), quantity, face value, market value, haircut value, net collateral value, settlement status, custodian, and — for exposure positions — exposure date, gross positive exposure (GPE), gross negative exposure (GNE), net current exposure (NCE), potential future exposure (PFE), threshold breach amount, collateral already posted/received, net margin requirement, and regulatory capital impact (CVA, RWA). Provides the real-time collateral inventory, margin exposure view feeding margin call generation, and regulatory reporting view (LCR HQLA pool, Basel III SA-CCR). SSOT for collateral positions and margin exposures.

attributes.name: accrued_interest
attributes.description: The interest accrued on the collateral asset (for interest-bearing securities or cash collateral) from the last coupon payment date to the position date. Included in net collateral value calculations.

attributes.name: collateral_posted_value
attributes.description: The total haircut-adjusted value of collateral already posted to the counterparty as of the position date. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: collateral_received_value
attributes.description: The total haircut-adjusted value of collateral received from the counterparty as of the position date. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: concentration_limit_breach
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this collateral position breaches concentration limits defined in the collateral agreement (e.g., maximum percentage of a single issuer or asset class).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this collateral position record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: credit_valuation_adjustment
attributes.description: The adjustment to the fair value of derivative positions to account for counterparty credit risk. Represents the market value of counterparty default risk. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Counterparty Credit Risk Capital Requirements (CVA Risk Capital Charge)

attributes.name: eligibility_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the collateral asset meets the eligibility criteria defined in the collateral agreement or regulatory framework: eligible (accepted), ineligible (rejected), restricted (conditionally accepted), pending_review (under evaluation).
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA) Eligible Collateral Schedule

attributes.name: exposure_date
attributes.description: For exposure-type positions, the date on which the counterparty credit exposure was calculated. Typically aligns with position_date but may differ for forward-looking exposure calculations.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

attributes.name: face_value
attributes.description: The nominal or par value of the collateral asset at issuance or contract inception, expressed in the asset's denomination currency.

attributes.name: gross_negative_exposure
attributes.description: The total mark-to-market value of all derivative and repo positions with the counterparty where the bank owes money, before netting or collateral offsets. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

attributes.name: gross_positive_exposure
attributes.description: The total mark-to-market value of all derivative and repo positions with the counterparty where the bank is owed money, before netting or collateral offsets. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

attributes.name: haircut_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage discount applied to the market value of the collateral to account for market risk, liquidity risk, and potential price volatility. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.15 for 15%).
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

attributes.name: haircut_value
attributes.description: The collateral value after applying the haircut percentage. Calculated as market_value * (1 - haircut_percentage). This is the risk-adjusted collateral value recognized for margin and capital purposes.
attributes.references: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: hqla_classification
attributes.description: The Basel III liquidity classification of the collateral asset: level_1 (highest quality, 0% haircut), level_2a (high quality, 15% haircut), level_2b (lower quality, 25-50% haircut), or non_hqla (not eligible for LCR).
attributes.references: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: independent_amount
attributes.description: An additional fixed or formula-based collateral amount required by one party regardless of current exposure, often used to cover potential future exposure or as initial margin. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: initial_margin
attributes.description: The upfront collateral required to cover potential future exposure over the margin period of risk, calculated using regulatory models (SIMM, grid-based) or internal models. Applicable to non-centrally cleared derivatives under margin reform rules.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) / International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives

attributes.name: market_value
attributes.description: The current fair market value of the collateral asset as of the position date, based on observable market prices or valuation models.
attributes.references: Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 820 Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: minimum_transfer_amount
attributes.description: The smallest increment of collateral that can be transferred under the collateral agreement. Collateral calls below this amount are not executed. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: net_collateral_value
attributes.description: The net value of collateral available after haircuts, accrued interest, fees, and any other adjustments. This is the effective collateral coverage amount.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: net_current_exposure
attributes.description: The net mark-to-market exposure after bilateral netting under a qualifying master netting agreement (e.g., ISDA Master Agreement). Calculated as max(GPE - GNE, 0). Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement

attributes.name: net_margin_requirement
attributes.description: The net amount of additional collateral required (positive) or excess collateral available for return (negative) after considering threshold, MTA, independent amount, and collateral already posted/received. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: position_date
attributes.description: The business date for which this collateral position snapshot is recorded. Represents the valuation date for inventory and exposure calculations.
attributes.references: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: position_type
attributes.description: Classification of the collateral position: held (owned but not pledged), posted (delivered to counterparty), received (accepted from counterparty), pledged (committed but not yet delivered), rehypothecated (received collateral reused), or exposure (calculated margin requirement record).
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

attributes.name: potential_future_exposure
attributes.description: An estimate of the maximum exposure that could arise in the future due to market movements, calculated using regulatory or internal models. Used for capital and margin calculations. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: The number of units or nominal amount of the collateral asset in this position. For securities, this is the number of shares or bonds; for cash, this is the principal amount.
attributes.references: International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) Standard ISO 6166

attributes.name: rehypothecation_allowed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the collateral receiver is permitted to rehypothecate (reuse) the received collateral under the terms of the collateral agreement.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: risk_weighted_assets
attributes.description: The regulatory capital requirement for this collateral position, calculated by applying risk weights to the exposure amount under Basel III standardized or internal ratings-based approaches. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel III Capital Requirements for Counterparty Credit Risk

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the collateral transfer was or is expected to be settled and ownership or control transferred.
attributes.references: Central Securities Depository Regulation (CSDR) Settlement Discipline

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: The current settlement state of the collateral position: pending (awaiting delivery), in_transit (delivery initiated), settled (delivery confirmed), failed (settlement did not complete), recalled (collateral substitution or return in progress).
attributes.references: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) MT 54x Series

attributes.name: substitution_right_exercised
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the collateral provider has exercised their right to substitute this collateral asset with another eligible asset under the terms of the CSA.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: threshold_amount
attributes.description: The minimum exposure level specified in the CSA or collateral agreement below which no collateral is required to be posted. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: threshold_breach_amount
attributes.description: The amount by which the net current exposure exceeds the threshold amount, triggering a margin call requirement. Calculated as max(NCE - threshold_amount, 0). Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Credit Support Annex (CSA)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this collateral position record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: variation_margin
attributes.description: The collateral exchanged daily to reflect changes in the mark-to-market value of derivative positions. Represents the current exposure component of margin. Applicable to exposure-type positions.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) / International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives

products.name: margin_exposure
products.description: Calculated exposure record representing the net mark-to-market exposure under a margin agreement or CSA, used to determine margin call obligations. Captures exposure date, gross positive exposure (GPE), gross negative exposure (GNE), net current exposure (NCE), potential future exposure (PFE), threshold breach amount, collateral already posted/received, net margin requirement, and regulatory capital impact (CVA, RWA). Feeds the margin call generation process.
products.reference: Net Current Exposure / NCE / MTM Exposure

attributes.name: margin_exposure_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the margin exposure calculation record.

attributes.name: margin_agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the margin agreement or Credit Support Annex (CSA) under which this exposure is calculated.

attributes.name: netting_set_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the group of transactions that are subject to bilateral netting under the ISDA Master Agreement. All trades within a netting set are netted together for exposure calculation.

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the counterparty entity with whom the margin exposure exists.
attributes.references: Basel III Counterparty Credit Risk Framework

attributes.name: settlement_deposit_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to account.deposit_account. Business justification: Margin exposure cash settlement: the deposit account used to fund or receive margin exposure settlements must be linked to the exposure record for intraday liquidity management, settlement failure mon

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: Liquidity stress testing projects margin calls under adverse scenarios. Stressed margin exposure drives liquidity buffer sizing and LCR/NSFR projections. Required for regulatory liquidity stress tests

attributes.name: stress_test_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_test_run. Business justification: Stressed margin exposure calculations are produced as part of stress test runs for CCAR/DFAST and counterparty credit risk stress testing. margin_exposure.stress_scenario_id already links to the scena

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to calculate the margin exposure and requirements. SIMM (Standard Initial Margin Model) is the industry standard for initial margin; other methods may be used for variation margin or under specific CSA terms.

attributes.name: calculation_run_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the batch calculation run that produced this exposure record. Used for audit trail and reconciliation purposes.

attributes.name: collateral_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the eligible collateral currency specified in the CSA. Determines the currency in which collateral must be posted.

attributes.name: collateral_posted_amount
attributes.description: The current market value of collateral that the bank has posted to the counterparty to cover exposure. Includes cash and securities adjusted for haircuts.

attributes.name: collateral_received_amount
attributes.description: The current market value of collateral that the bank has received from the counterparty to cover their exposure to the bank. Includes cash and securities adjusted for haircuts.

attributes.name: collateral_segregation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether initial margin collateral must be held in a segregated account at a third-party custodian, as required by regulatory mandates for certain counterparties and jurisdictions.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this margin exposure record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: cva_amount
attributes.description: The adjustment to the fair value of derivative positions to account for counterparty credit risk. Represents the market value of counterparty default risk and is used for regulatory capital calculations.
attributes.references: Basel III CVA Risk Capital Charge

attributes.name: dispute_threshold_amount
attributes.description: The minimum exposure difference amount that can trigger a formal dispute resolution process under the CSA. Valuation differences below this amount are typically resolved informally.

attributes.name: dva_amount
attributes.description: The adjustment to the fair value of derivative positions to account for the bank's own credit risk. Represents the benefit the bank receives from its own default risk.

attributes.name: ead_amount
attributes.description: The estimated exposure amount at the time of counterparty default, used for regulatory capital calculations. Incorporates current exposure and potential future exposure.

attributes.name: exposure_date
attributes.description: The business date on which this margin exposure was calculated, typically the valuation date for mark-to-market positions.

attributes.name: exposure_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when the margin exposure calculation was performed, including time zone information.

attributes.name: gne_amount
attributes.description: The total mark-to-market value of all positions where the bank has a negative exposure to the counterparty (bank owes the counterparty). Represents the gross liability before netting and collateral.
attributes.references: Basel III Counterparty Credit Risk - SA-CCR

attributes.name: gpe_amount
attributes.description: The total mark-to-market value of all positions where the bank has a positive exposure to the counterparty (counterparty owes the bank). Represents the gross amount at risk before netting and collateral.
attributes.references: Basel III Counterparty Credit Risk - SA-CCR

attributes.name: independent_amount
attributes.description: Additional collateral required beyond the current exposure, often used as a buffer for potential future exposure or as initial margin. Also known as Initial Margin (IM) under regulatory frameworks.
attributes.references: Basel III Initial Margin Requirements for Non-Cleared Derivatives

attributes.name: initial_margin_amount
attributes.description: The collateral amount required to cover potential future exposure over the margin period of risk, calculated using regulatory models (SIMM) or internal models. Required for non-cleared derivatives under regulatory mandates.

attributes.name: last_margin_call_date
attributes.description: The date on which the most recent margin call was issued for this margin agreement and counterparty.

attributes.name: margin_call_direction
attributes.description: Indicates the direction of the margin call: whether the bank is calling for collateral from the counterparty, the counterparty is calling from the bank, or no call is required.

attributes.name: margin_call_status
attributes.description: The current status of the margin call process for this exposure calculation. Tracks whether a margin call has been issued, satisfied, or is in dispute.

attributes.name: margin_period_of_risk_days
attributes.description: The number of days between the last margin call and the closeout of positions following a counterparty default. Used in calculating initial margin requirements. Typically 10 days for standard CSAs.
attributes.references: Basel III Margin Period of Risk Definition

attributes.name: minimum_transfer_amount
attributes.description: The minimum amount of collateral that must be transferred in a single margin call. Margin calls below this amount are not executed to reduce operational burden.
attributes.references: ISDA CSA Minimum Transfer Amount Definition

attributes.name: nce_amount
attributes.description: The net mark-to-market exposure after bilateral netting of all positions under the margin agreement. Calculated as GPE minus GNE. Positive values indicate the bank is owed; negative values indicate the bank owes.

attributes.name: net_collateral_position
attributes.description: The net collateral position calculated as collateral received minus collateral posted. Positive values indicate the bank holds net collateral; negative values indicate the bank has posted net collateral.

attributes.name: net_margin_requirement
attributes.description: The net amount of additional collateral required to be posted or returned based on the current exposure, threshold, and existing collateral. Positive values indicate the bank must post more collateral; negative values indicate the bank can request collateral return.

attributes.name: next_margin_call_date
attributes.description: The next scheduled date on which a margin call may be issued based on the CSA terms. Typically daily for most CSAs but may be less frequent for certain counterparties.

attributes.name: pfe_amount
attributes.description: The estimated maximum exposure that could arise in the future due to market movements, calculated using regulatory or internal models. Used for regulatory capital calculations and risk management.
attributes.references: Basel III SA-CCR Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk

attributes.name: regulatory_im_model
attributes.description: The regulatory model used to calculate initial margin requirements. SIMM (Standard Initial Margin Model) is the industry standard; grid and schedule are simplified approaches; internal models require regulatory approval.

attributes.name: rwa_amount
attributes.description: The risk-weighted asset amount calculated for this exposure under Basel III regulatory capital requirements. Used to determine the capital charge for counterparty credit risk.
attributes.references: Basel III Standardized Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name of the upstream system that calculated or provided this margin exposure data (e.g., Murex, Calypso, SAS Risk Management).

attributes.name: threshold_amount
attributes.description: The contractual threshold amount specified in the CSA below which no margin call is required. Exposure must exceed this amount before collateral posting obligations are triggered.

attributes.name: threshold_breach_amount
attributes.description: The amount by which the net current exposure exceeds the contractual threshold. This is the exposure amount that triggers a margin call obligation. Calculated as NCE minus threshold amount (if positive).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this margin exposure record was last modified or recalculated.

attributes.name: valuation_agent
attributes.description: Identifies which party is responsible for calculating the exposure valuation under the CSA terms. May be the bank, counterparty, a third-party service, or bilateral (both parties calculate independently).

attributes.name: variation_margin_amount
attributes.description: The collateral amount required to cover the current mark-to-market exposure, calculated daily based on changes in position values. Distinct from initial margin which covers potential future exposure.
attributes.references: Basel III Margin Requirements for Non-Cleared Derivatives

Distinct from CSA (derivatives) and GMRA (repo) — covers secured commercial lending collateral.

products.name: liquidity_position
products.description: Daily intraday and end-of-day liquidity position and forward cash flow forecast for the bank, capturing available liquid assets, cash balances across nostro accounts, central bank reserves, undrawn committed facilities, and projected inflows/outflows by currency and tenor bucket (intraday, overnight, 1W, 2W, 1M, 3M). Distinguishes contractual cash flows (loan repayments, bond maturities, coupon payments) from behavioral cash flows (deposit runoff, credit line drawdowns) under base and stress scenarios. Includes forward-looking cash flow forecast by business line for liquidity stress testing and contingency funding planning. Serves as the operational heartbeat for ALCO and treasury desk liquidity monitoring. Tracks LCR and NSFR buffer positions against regulatory minimums (Basel III / BCBS). Supports intraday liquidity monitoring per BCBS 248 and contingency funding trigger assessment. Post-merge: this is the single source of truth for liquidity positions and cash flow forecasting — replaces former separate cash_flow_forecast product.

products.name: liquidity_ratio
products.description: Unified regulatory liquidity ratio record capturing both Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) and Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) calculations per legal entity and consolidated group. For LCR: captures HQLA stock, total net cash outflows over a 30-day stress horizon, and resulting LCR percentage. For NSFR: captures Available Stable Funding (ASF), Required Stable Funding (RSF) by asset/liability category, and resulting NSFR percentage. Supports daily and quarterly regulatory reporting to the Federal Reserve and OCC under Basel III. Tracks breaches, buffers, and trends against the 100% minimum thresholds for both ratios. Includes ratio type discriminator (LCR, NSFR) for unified compliance monitoring.

attributes.description: The calculated NSFR expressed as a percentage. Calculated as (Available Stable Funding / Required Stable Funding) * 100. Regulatory minimum is 100%.

attributes.name: period_over_period_change_percentage

attributes.name: prior_period_ratio_percentage

attributes.name: ratio_type
attributes.description: Discriminator indicating the type of liquidity ratio: LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio) for 30-day stress horizon or NSFR (Net Stable Funding Ratio) for one-year structural funding stability.

attributes.name: record_status

attributes.name: regulatory_threshold_percentage
attributes.description: The regulatory minimum threshold for the ratio (typically 100% for both LCR and NSFR under Basel III).

attributes.name: reporting_date

attributes.name: submission_date

attributes.description: Total stock of HQLA after applying haircuts and caps. Numerator of the LCR calculation.

attributes.description: Total expected net cash outflows over the 30-day stress scenario. Denominator of the LCR calculation.

products.name: ftp_rate
products.description: Comprehensive Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP) product covering the full FTP lifecycle: internal transfer pricing curve construction, rate definition, and account-level allocation. Curve construction: term structure of internal transfer rates by currency, tenor, and curve type (base rate, liquidity spread, credit spread), built from market benchmarks (SOFR, OIS, swap rates) adjusted for bank-specific liquidity premiums, versioned by effective date and ALCO approval. Rate definition: FTP rates assigned to asset and liability products by tenor bucket, currency, and product type, capturing methodology (matched-maturity, pooled, hybrid), base rate index, spread components (liquidity premium, optionality charge, basis adjustment). Allocation: transactional FTP charge/credit records applied to individual loan, deposit, and investment accounts with notional balance, FTP rate, FTP amount, calculation date, and business line cost center. Enables NIM decomposition and RAROC calculation at product, segment, and LOB level. Post-merge: this is the single source of truth for all FTP methodology, curves, rates, and allocations — replaces former separate transfer_pricing_curve and ftp_allocation products.

products.name: capital_ratio
products.description: Regulatory capital adequacy and planning record capturing current capital ratios (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital), Risk-Weighted Assets by risk type (credit, market, operational), leverage ratio, and capital buffers (conservation, countercyclical, G-SIB surcharge) at legal entity and consolidated level. Includes multi-year capital planning: projected CET1 trajectories, RWA growth assumptions, dividend/buyback plans, stress scenario capital paths, and capital actions (issuance, redemption, AT1 triggers) under base and adverse scenarios. Produced for CCAR, DFAST, and Basel III Pillar 1 regulatory submissions. Tracks ALCO-approved capital targets and management buffers above regulatory minimums. Post-merge: this is the single source of truth for capital ratios and capital planning — replaces former separate capital_plan product. Note: potential SSOT overlap with risk domain capital/RWA products requires global architect adjudication.

products.name: nostro_account
products.description: Master record and daily reconciliation for the banks nostro accounts held at correspondent banks globally. Master attributes: account number, correspondent bank BIC/SWIFT, currency, account purpose (settlement, FX, securities), authorized signatories, overdraft limit, account status. Reconciliation attributes: daily matching of internal ledger balances against correspondent bank statements (MT940/MT950), matched/unmatched items (breaks), break aging by category, reconciliation status, resolution actions, and escalation triggers. Critical for RTGS and SWIFT payment settlement, FX position management, and intraday liquidity monitoring (BCBS 248). Regulatory requirement under OCC guidance on correspondent banking controls. Post-merge: this is the single source of truth for nostro master data and reconciliation — replaces former separate nostro_reconciliation product.
